items.title: Quantitative KRAS ctDNA Dynamics Predict Early Recurrence After Neoadjuvant Therapy and Surgery in Pancreatic Cancer
items.abstract: Early recurrence remains prevalent in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) despite multimodality treatment. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is an emerging prognostic biomarker showing promise in detecting minimal residual disease (MRD). Using a high-sensitivity digital droplet PCR (ddPCR) assay, we evaluated KRAS- mutant ctDNA as a marker of MRD associated with early recurrence (< 12 months) in patients with localized PDAC receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC), surgery, and adjuvant chemotherapy (AC). KRAS G12D, G12V, and G12R mutations found in cell-free DNA were detected and quantified with maximum variant allele frequency (mVAF). Of 130 enrolled patients, 55 completed NAC and resection. ctDNA was detected a median of 7.6 months before imaging-confirmed recurrence. Postoperative detection KRAS ctDNA was independently associated with worse recurrence-free survival (RFS) (aHR 3.30, 95% CI 1.33–8.21, p = 0.010), and ctDNA clearance after NAC and surgery was independently associated with improved RFS (aHR 0.23, 95% CI 0.06–0.90, p = 0.035). Median cohort mVAF was 0.03%; patients with mVAF above the median had shorter RFS (12.8 vs. 26.3 months) and more frequent early recurrence (p = 0.027). ctDNA-positive patients who received AC remained with worse outcomes than ctDNA-negative patients, suggesting persistent chemotherapy resistance. These data indicated that persistent KRAS ctDNA after NAC and surgery reflects MRD and support sensitive postoperative ctDNA testing to stratify high risk patients for early recurrence, guiding quantitative, longitudinal monitoring. Future studies in adaptive treatment settings may further extend these findings toward ctDNA-guided clinical decision-making.

items.title: Real-world analysis of treatment sequencing and late-stage liquid biopsy genomic profiling in advanced pancreatic cancer
items.abstract: Background Real-world evidence on treatment sequencing and the molecular features of terminal-stage pancreatic cancer is limited. We evaluated treatment sequences and late-stage liquid biopsy genomic profiles using a nationwide clinico-genomic database. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 16,782 patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma registered in the Center for Cancer Genomics and Advanced Therapeutics database in Japan. Overall survival was compared according to first-line regimen and first- to second-line sequence. Liquid biopsy data were analyzed in relation to the time before death, and a gradient-boosting survival model was developed to identify prognostic genomic features. Results As first-line therapy, gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel was associated with longer overall survival than FOLFIRINOX (hazard ratio 0.89, 95% confidence interval 0.84–0.93), despite comparable time to treatment failure. Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel followed by FOLFIRINOX was associated with the most favorable survival, measured from either first-line (hazard ratio 0.84) or second-line initiation (hazard ratio 0.68). Liquid biopsies were performed closer to death than tissue-based tests (median 140 vs. 473 days). The KRAS variant allele frequency increased as death approached and was the most influential prognostic feature; a KRAS -only model performed comparably to the full model (concordance index 0.67 for both), and survival worsened with increasing KRAS variant allele frequency. Alterations in chromatin-remodeling and epigenetic regulatory genes, including SMARCA4 , ARID1A , KDM6A , and KMT2D , were associated with poor prognosis. Conclusion Treatment sequencing may influence survival in advanced pancreatic cancer, and the KRAS variant allele frequency in late-stage liquid biopsy is a robust prognostic biomarker.

items.title: Methylene blue modulates G3BP1-associated condensation and attenuates Kras-driven pancreatic preneoplastic lesions
items.abstract: Abstract Stress granules (SGs) are dynamic biomolecular condensates implicated in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), with G3BP1/2 serving as key regulators of their assembly. We combined structure-based screening of FDA-approved drugs with cellular and biochemical assays and identified methylene blue (MB) as a modulator of SG assembly. MB suppressed SG accumulation across multiple PDAC cell lines under arsenite (AS)-induced stress, nutrient deprivation, and heat shock without reducing the abundance of major SG-associated proteins. In reconstituted systems, MB inhibited G3BP1 condensation with or without added RNA and showed a nonsignificant trend toward lower G3BP1-Caprin1 co-immunoprecipitation in cells. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations predicted a potential MB interaction site within the G3BP1 NTF2-like (NTF2L) domain. The G3BP1 V11A/F15A/F33A/F124A mutant retained basal condensate-forming capacity but showed reduced responsiveness to MB compared with wild-type G3BP1, implicating this region in MB-mediated regulation. In Kras-driven KC mice, chronic oral MB administration was associated with reduced pancreatic G3BP1-positive puncta, increased acinar preservation, and decreased preneoplastic lesion burden, epithelial proliferation, and stromal remodeling, without overt abnormalities in the evaluated endpoints. Together, these findings identify MB as a small-molecule probe that modulates G3BP1 condensation dynamics and demonstrate that chronic MB treatment is associated with the attenuation of early Kras driven pancreatic preneoplastic lesion progression in vivo.

items.title: FOXO3a suppression predicts poor prognosis and facilitates cell migration and invasion through the WNT/β-catenin pathway in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Forkhead box O3a (FOXO3a) plays important roles in tumor development; however, its expression pattern, prognostic significance, and biological function in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remain unclear.
METHODS: FOXO3a expression was evaluated in PDAC tissues and correlated with clinicopathological characteristics and patient survival. FOXO3a-overexpressing and FOXO3a-silenced PDAC cell models were established to investigate its actions on cell growth, migratory capacity, and invasiveness. The participation of the WNT/β-catenin pathway was examined using immunofluorescence, Western blotting, and rescue experiments. Xenograft models were employed to validate the impact of FOXO3a in regulating in vivo tumor growth.
RESULTS: FOXO3a expression was significantly reduced across both PDAC tissue specimens and cell lines compared with controls. Decreased FOXO3a expression was correlated with advanced tumor stage (P = 0.008), perineural invasion (P = 0.019), and distant metastatic status (P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses demonstrated that low FOXO3a expression independently predicted poor overall survival (HR = 2.068, P = 0.004). High β-catenin expression was also identified as an independent risk factor of poor patient outcome (HR = 1.827, P = 0.014). Functionally, FOXO3a overexpression inhibited PDAC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, whereas FOXO3a depletion promoted malignant behaviors. Mechanistically, FOXO3a suppressed the WNT/β-catenin signaling by decreasing the nuclear accumulation of β-catenin, and pathway activation partially reversed FOXO3a-mediated inhibition. In vivo, FOXO3a overexpression significantly inhibited xenograft growth.
CONCLUSION: FOXO3a downregulation exhibits a significant correlation with dverse clinicopathological features and unfavorable outcome in PDAC. FOXO3a exerts tumor-suppressive effects, at least in part, by negatively regulating the WNT/β-catenin pathway and consequently holds promise as a prognostic marker and targeted therapy for PDAC.

items.title: Randomized multicentre Phase 2 clinical trial of non-viral gene therapy for pancreatic cancer: clinical and molecular findings.
items.abstract: Aim: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has a dismal prognosis, and innovative therapies are needed. We developed a phase I pilot, non-viral gene therapy (CYL-02) encoding SST2 and DCK::UMK genes complexed with a polyethyleneimine non-viral vector to sensitize tumours to gemcitabine chemotherapy, which showed excellent feasibility and safety. Methods: An open-label, multicentre, randomized Phase 2 trial (NCT02806687) compared CYL-02 [two intratumoral endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided injections one month apart] + gemcitabine injected weekly vs. gemcitabine alone in 70 patients (n = 35 per arm) with locally advanced PDAC. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints were overall survival (OS), tumour response, safety, and ancillary studies. Results: PFS did not differ between arms. Unexpectedly, OS was worse in the gene therapy + chemotherapy arm. Exploratory analyses revealed no differences in clinical status, baseline characteristics, or the number of patients receiving second-line therapy, with the exception of a more frequent use of FOLFOX post-progression in the control arm, which could explain this difference. Proteomic profiling identified clusterin (CLU) as a candidate treatment-induced resistance factor in patients: CYL-02 + gemcitabine significantly increased circulating CLU levels, while gemcitabine alone did not. In vitro and in vivo models confirmed CLU induction by DCK combined with gemcitabine and demonstrated that CLU silencing restored chemosensitivity, reducing experimental tumour volume in mice. Conclusion: CLU induction in patients receiving CYL-02 and gemcitabine may explain adaptive resistance and lack of efficacy of gene therapy. These results provide a rationale for combining CYL-02 and gemcitabine with CLU targeting to overcome resistance in pancreatic cancer.

items.title: CT-Based Radiomics for Preoperative Prediction of Surgical Margins in Pancreatic Head Cancer: A Tool for Selecting Patients for Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microscopic margin involvement (≤ 1 mm) strongly predicts poor prognosis in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) after upfront resection fails to fully mitigate this risk. It remains uncertain whether neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) can neutralize the adverse prognostic impact of impending ≤ 1 mm margins.
METHODS: Prognostic significance of ≤ 1 mm margins was assessed in an upfront-resection cohort (n = 228) using multivariable Cox regression. A separate cohort (n = 110; 52 NACT, 58 upfront surgery) compared overall survival (OS) by margin status. A CT-based radiomics model using a Laplacian-Dirichlet operator was developed to predict ≤ 1 mm margins and externally validated (n = 230).
RESULTS: ≤ 1 mm margins independently predicted worse OS vs. > 1 mm (15.0 vs. 24.0 months, p = 0.005). ACT numerically extended OS for ≤ 1 mm patients (16.0 vs. 15.0 months, p = 0.271) but did not close the survival gap. Notably, ≤ 1 mm patients receiving NACT achieved median OS of 29.4 months-comparable to > 1 mm upfront patients (31.6 months)-and significantly better than ≤ 1 mm upfront patients (19.6 months, p = 0.045). The model predicted ≤ 1 mm margins with AUCs of 0.772 (95% CI: 0.705-0.838) and 0.723 (95% CI: 0.657-0.789) in internal and external validation.
CONCLUSION: NACT-not ACT-selectively rescues high-risk patients destined for ≤ 1 mm margins. Our radiomics model enables preoperative identification, supporting personalized neoadjuvant therapy.

items.title: Treatment Response and Oncologic Outcomes Following Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Switch in Localized Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Many patients undergoing neoadjuvant therapy for localized pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) experience treatment intolerance or disease progression during initial therapy. Although chemotherapy switch is increasingly utilized, response rates and oncologic outcomes remain poorly defined.
METHODS: Patients were identified from a prospectively maintained database of individuals undergoing neoadjuvant therapy for localized PDAC from 2012 to 2023. Eligible patients underwent chemotherapy switch between 5-fluorouracil and gemcitabine regimens with curative intent. Favorable response was defined as complete or partial radiographic response by RECIST, or stable disease with a ≥ 50% decline in CA 19-9 relative to levels before switch. Outcomes were measured from the date of chemotherapy switch.
RESULTS: Out of 161 patients, 41% achieved favorable response. Body/tail, borderline resectable, and locally advanced disease were independently associated with nonfavorable response. Among favorable responders, 49% underwent resection versus 11% of nonresponders. Favorable response was independently associated with improved progression-free and overall survival, including among unresected patients. Overall, 47% derived meaningful oncologic benefit through favorable response, resection, or both.
CONCLUSIONS: Chemotherapy switch offers a reasonable strategy in select patients with localized PDAC experiencing inadequate response or intolerance of initial therapy. This composite response framework identifies chemosensitive tumor biology, informs surgical decision-making, and stratifies prognosis.

items.title: Current and emerging strategies to enhance chemotherapeutic efficacy in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic cancer remains one of the most aggressive solid malignancies. The majority of patients present with locally advanced or metastatic disease, limiting treatment options to systemic chemotherapy. Conventional chemotherapy forms the backbone of the standard-of-care regimen and offers modest but significant survival benefits.
MAIN BODY: This review discusses currently established standard-of-care regimens and cutting edge clinical trials which aim to enhance chemotherapy efficacy in pancreatic cancer. Pancreatic cancer's distinct pathological features-including its high metastatic potential, inherent chemoresistance, dense desmoplastic stroma, and profoundly immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment-underscore the rationale for the clinical development of chemosensitizing agents. As mechanisms of chemoresistance continue to be uncovered, new therapeutic avenues are emerging that aim to enhance the efficacy of chemotherapy. Emerging targets including KRAS, MTAP, EGFR, Claudin 18.2, and WEE1, which present unique vulnerabilities for rational combination therapies, are discussed.
CONCLUSION: Given the central role of chemotherapy in pancreatic cancer treatment, ongoing clinical strategies that improve its efficacy are essential to achieving better outcomes for patients.

items.title: Distal Pancreatectomy in Octogenarians and the Role of Robotic Surgery.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A minimally invasive approach currently is the gold standard for distal pancreatectomy (DP). Robotic distal pancreatectomy (RDP) is increasingly adopted and offers technical advantages. As life expectancy rises, more octogenarians undergo pancreatic resection, and emerging evidence suggests minimally invasive approaches may benefit older adults. However, the role of RDP in this population remains underexplored.
METHODS: A multi-institutional retrospective cohort study from four high-volume North American hepato-pancreatobiliary centers was conducted. Adults undergoing elective open distal pancreatectomy (ODP) or RDP between 2007 and 2023 were stratified as < 80 versus ≥ 80 years of age. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality. The secondary outcomes included major complications and oncologic outcomes. Multivariable models were applied to adjust for relevant covariates. A subanalysis was performed on patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC).
RESULTS: Of 797 patients undergoing DP, 62 were aged ≥ 80 years. Despite more comorbidities and higher PDAC rates, older patients had comparable perioperative outcomes. Blood loss, conversion, complications, length of stay, readmissions, and 90-day mortality were similar between age groups. On adjusted analysis, age ≥ 80 years was not associated with major complications or 90-day mortality in the overall cohort or PDAC subgroup. Whereas RDP was independently associated with fewer major complications, longer operative time and greater blood loss increased adverse outcomes. Among PDAC patients, perioperative and oncologic outcomes, including survival, were comparable across age groups.
CONCLUSION: Octogenarians achieve perioperative and oncologic outcomes comparable with those of younger patients when treated in high-volume centers, including survival. A robotic approach proved advantageous in reducing complications. The current findings reinforce the role of resection when indicated.

items.title: Study of MC001 in Patients With Advanced Solid Tumours
items.abstract:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of MC001 and to determine the appropriate dose for further development in adults with advanced solid tumours, with expansion cohorts in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What is the maximum tolerated dose (MTD), maximum administered dose (MAD), and recommended dose for expansion (RDE) of MC001?
* How does MC001 behave in the body following single and multiple doses?
* Does MC001 show preliminary antitumour activity in patients with PDAC and NPC?
* What are the pharmacodynamic effects of MC001?
* What medical problems do participants have when taking MC001?

Research participants will:

* Receive MC001 every 21 days until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, or at the investigator's discretion.
* Visit the clinic every 21 days for drug administration, biopsy, and assessments including blood tests, eye tests, and imaging.

items.title: A Multicenter, Prospective Single-arm Study of Multimodal Thermal Therapy Combined With Toripalimab and AG Chemotherapy in the Treatment of Advanced Pancreatic Cancer
items.abstract: This study is a multicenter, prospective, single-arm, open-label, Simon two-stage phase II clinical trial designed to evaluate the conversion therapeutic value of multimodal thermal therapy combined with TIS (Toripalimab) and AG chemotherapy (gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel) in previously untreated metastatic pancreatic cancer patients with liver-only or lung-only metastases.

items.title: Ras signaling in cancer: From molecular mechanisms to next-generation therapeutic inhibitors.
items.abstract: RAS proteins are small GTP-binding molecular switches that integrate extracellular signals from growth factors, cytokines, and hormones to coordinate key cellular processes. RAS signaling is tightly regulated to maintain tissue homeostasis and ensure precise developmental control. However, dysregulation of this pathway-drives oncogenic transformation, tumor progression, and resistance to therapy. Despite decades of intensive investigation, RAS-driven malignancies remain among the most difficult cancers to treat, highlighting the urgent need for updated perspectives that integrate recent mechanistic insights with rapidly advancing therapeutic strategies. Notably, recent breakthroughs-including mutation-specific inhibitors such as KRAS(G12C) inhibitors and emerging agents such as RMC-7977 and RMC-6236 that selectively target the active RAS conformation-have revitalized the field and underscore the importance of a comprehensive and timely review. In this article, we provide an in-depth overview of RAS signaling, beginning with its molecular mechanisms in normal cellular physiology and progressing to its multifaceted roles in cancer initiation, progression, and chemoresistance. We further summarize current advances in the development of direct RAS-targeted therapeutics, with particular emphasis on the emerging pan-RAS (ON) inhibitors RMC-7977 and RMC-6236, and discuss their potential therapeutic implications particularly in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and non-small-cell lung cancer. Finally, we highlight key challenges for translating RAS(ON) inhibition into durable clinical benefit, including patient selection, biomarker development, early detection and mechanistic understanding of resistance, and rational combination strategies. Collectively, advances in mutation-selective and RAS(ON)-directed therapies are transforming RAS from a historically "undruggable" oncogenic driver into an increasingly tractable target in precision oncology.

items.title: daNIS-2: a phase III, randomized, double-blind study of the anti-TGF-β monoclonal antibody NIS793 or placebo in combination with nab-paclitaxel/gemcitabine as first-line treatment in patients with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This phase III, randomized, double-blind study (daNIS-2) evaluated the efficacy and safety of NIS793, an anti-transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) monoclonal antibody, in combination with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel [standard of care (SOC)] versus placebo and SOC as first-line treatment in patients with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (mPDAC).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: The study included a safety run-in (n = 21 patients enrolled) followed by a randomized part (n = 490 patients randomly assigned). Patients were assigned 1 : 1 to receive NIS793 or placebo with SOC. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS), secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), overall response rate (ORR), safety, pharmacokinetics, and exploratory biomarker analyses.
RESULTS: The study was terminated early following an interim analysis due to an unfavorable benefit-risk profile. Median OS was 9.2 months in the NIS793 arm versus 11.2 months in the placebo arm (hazard ratio 1.26, 95% confidence interval 1.01-1.59). The estimates of ORR and median PFS indicate a less favorable treatment effect with NIS793. Safety profiles were comparable between arms, although higher rates of anemia, epistaxis, and rash were observed with NIS793; serious adverse events were more frequent in the NIS793 arm, with most being grade ≥3. Pharmacodynamic markers such as Pro-C3 supported target engagement. However, such target engagement did not translate into clinical benefit and early circulating tumor DNA dynamics were associated with less favorable outcomes. Biomarker analyses suggested that unfavorable benefit-risk profile of NIS793 was most pronounced in patients with a low epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition signature and a classical molecular subtype.
CONCLUSIONS: NIS793 in combination with SOC did not improve survival outcomes in first-line mPDAC and was associated with an unfavorable benefit-risk profile. Exploratory biomarker findings highlight the complexity of TGF-β signaling and underscore the need for refined patient selection strategies in future trials.

items.title: Real-World Tolerability and Effectiveness of Nanoliposomal Irinotecan in Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer: A Multicentre Indian Experience.
items.abstract: Background Metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (mPDAC) is associated with poor prognosis and has limited therapeutic options. Nanoliposomal irinotecan (Nal-IRI), evaluated in the NAPOLI-1 and NAPOLI-3 clinical trials, has demonstrated survival benefit in later-line and first-line settings, respectively. However, real-world data, particularly from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) such as India, remain limited. We aimed to evaluate the real-world tolerability and early effectiveness of nal-IRI-based regimens in Indian patients with mPDAC. Methods This multicentre, retrospective observational study included 24 patients with histologically confirmed mPDAC treated with nal-IRI-based regimens (either nal-IRI + 5-FU/LV or nal-IRI + 5-FU/LV + oxaliplatin) between June 2024 and September 2025. The primary objective was to assess tolerability using CTCAE v5.0-graded adverse events (AEs). Secondary objectives included early effectiveness outcomes, assessed by overall survival (OS) using the Kaplan-Meier method. Restricted mean survival time (RMST) was calculated at three- and six-month landmarks due to limited follow-up. Results The mean age was 63.7 years (SD 6.89), and 75% of patients were male. Nal-IRI was administered in the first-line setting in six patients and in second or later lines in 18 patients. The median follow-up was four months. A total of 55 AEs were reported, most commonly diarrhea (20%), fatigue (12.7%), and mucositis and neutropenia (10.9% each). Among graded events, 26.4% were grade 1, 39.6% were grade 2, and 34.0% were grade 3. Dose modifications were required in 36.5% of events, and treatment discontinuation due to AEs occurred in 11.5% of events. Kaplan-Meier-estimated OS probabilities at three and six months were 95% and 88%, respectively, with an RMST of 2.89 months up to three months and 5.57 months up to six months. Conclusions In this multicentre real-world Indian cohort, nal-IRI-based regimens demonstrated manageable tolerability. These findings support the feasibility of nal-IRI in routine clinical practice and provide important real-world evidence (RWE) from an underrepresented population. However, survival outcomes were exploratory because of the short follow-up and high degree of censoring. Larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are warranted.

items.title: Endoscopic Ultrasound Shear Wave Elastography in Solid Pancreatic Lesions
items.abstract: The aim of this prospective study is to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of endoscopic ultrasound-guided shear wave elastography (EUS-SWE) in patients with solid pancreatic lesions. During a clinically indicated EUS with fine-needle biopsy, tissue stiffness will be measured by shear wave elastography in the pancreatic lesion and in the adjacent normal pancreatic parenchyma. Elastography values will be compared with the final cytological/histological diagnosis in order to assess the ability of EUS-SWE to differentiate malignant from benign lesions and to correlate stiffness with histological findings.

items.title: An asymmetric split-costimulatory MSLN.BBz/NKG2D.28 dual CAR-T design enhances activity against antigenically heterogeneous pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains a highly lethal solid tumor with limited responsiveness to chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy. A major challenge is antigen heterogeneity, which allows antigen-low or antigen-negative tumor cells to escape immune pressure. Here, we identified mesothelin (MSLN) and NKG2D ligands (NKG2DLs) as a complementary antigen pair in PDAC, showing frequent but discordant expression in clinical specimens. Based on this, we generated single-target, tandem, and dual CAR constructs against MSLN and/or NKG2DLs and compared their antitumor activity. Among them, an asymmetric split-costimulatory dual-CAR, MSLN.BBz/NKG2D.28, showed the best overall performance. MSLN.BBz/NKG2D.28 CAR-T cells efficiently eliminated single-positive, double-positive, and mixed-antigen tumor populations, sustained serial killing, produced higher effector cytokines, and preserved a less exhausted, more memory-like phenotype in vitro. In vivo, MSLN.BBz/NKG2D.28 CAR-T achieved stronger tumor control, greater intratumoral accumulation, improved persistence, and prolonged survival in pancreatic tumor models, including those mimicking antigen heterogeneity. Transcriptomic, biochemical, and pharmacologic analyses further identified IL-2-STAT5 signaling as an important pathway supporting the enhanced fitness and antitumor activity of this construct. Together, these findings show that dual targeting alone is insufficient; the arrangement of receptor inputs and costimulatory signals strongly influences therapeutic output. This study identifies MSLN.BBz/NKG2D.28 as a promising dual-CAR strategy for PDAC.

items.title: High-Sensitivity Detection of Early Pancreatic Cancer Using a Structured Scoring System Among Clinically Selected Outpatients: A Nationwide Prospective Study.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To prospectively evaluate the diagnostic performance of a structured scoring system integrating multiple pancreatic cancer (PC)-relevant factors for detecting early-stage PC among clinically selected outpatients.
METHODS: In this nationwide multicenter prospective cohort study, consecutive physician-selected outpatients undergoing initial endoscopic ultrasonography for mild symptoms, risk factors, or subtle imaging abnormalities were enrolled. Risk factors were categorized as low- or high-grade relevance (LGR/HGR), with one point per factor. A positive score was defined as LGR ≥ 3 and/or HGR ≥ 1. Diagnostic performance for high-grade dysplasia (HGD)/stage 1 PC was compared with that of conventional symptom-, family history-, and genetic risk-based approaches within this cohort.
RESULTS: Among 3269 patients, 2525 were score-positive and 744 were score-negative. For HGD/stage 1 PC, the sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 93.2%, 23.1%, 2.7%, and 99.3%, respectively. Sensitivity significantly exceeded that of conventional approaches (93.2% vs. 56.8%, p < 0.001), although paired comparison using the conditional relative odds ratio (CROR) showed no significant difference (CROR, 1.79; 95% CI, 0.54-5.90; p = 0.34). HGD/stage 1 PC detection was significantly higher in score-positive than in score-negative patients (2.7% vs. 0.7%, p = 0.001). Among PCs detected in score-positive patients, 24.3% were HGD/stage 1.
CONCLUSIONS: The scoring system demonstrated high cross-sectional sensitivity for HGD/stage 1 PC detection among clinically selected outpatients undergoing detailed PC evaluation. Its utility for selecting patients from unselected general outpatient populations remains unestablished. Prospective validation in consecutive general outpatients with systematic longitudinal follow-up is warranted.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered in the University Hospital Medical Network Clinical Trials Registry (http://www.umin.ac.jp/ctr/index.htm) as UMIN000034832 on December 1, 2018.

items.title: Unifying functional experimental systems with clinical predictive technologies for personalized care in PDAC.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains a clinical challenge, projected to become the second leading cause of cancer-related death by 2030. Traditional research has historically relied on established PDAC-derived cell lines to establish 2D in vitro models or in vivo xenografts for drug discovery. These approaches, however, fail to encompass the complexity of PDAC and few studies have been translated into game-changing treatments for patients with pancreatic cancer. This review advocates for a paradigm shift through the integration of complementary modeling strategies. We provide a comprehensive evaluation of more sophisticated in vitro systems, such as 3D models (spheroids and organoids), co-cultures and microfluidics, which offer scalable platforms for high-throughput screening and mechanistic analysis. Likewise, we emphasize the indispensable role of in vivo models, including genetically engineered mouse models (GEMMs) for studying stepwise progression and immune evasion, and patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) for capturing human-specific drug sensitivities and intratumoral heterogeneity. Beyond functional models, we explore the clinical utility of transcriptomic profiling to define PDAC subtypes, facilitating real-time patient stratification in landmark clinical trials. We further examine the role of liquid biopsy as a dynamic tool for monitoring minimal residual disease and the emergence of treatment resistance. Finally, we discuss the future of pharmacogenomics, the "tri-genomic" influence of the microbiome, and the integration of multi-omics through artificial intelligence to optimize individual therapeutic outcomes. By unifying these diverse predictive paradigms, we aim to bridge the gap between preclinical discovery and precision oncology, fostering more effective and individualized treatment strategies for all PDAC patients.

items.title: ACSL5 suppresses pancreatic cancer progression and gemcitabine resistance by regulating n-6 docosapentaenoic acid metabolism.
items.abstract: Gemcitabine (GEM) resistance remains a major challenge in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) treatment. Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of tumors, and imbalance in lipid metabolism promotes tumor progression and drug resistance. This study aims to elucidate the mechanism of Acyl-CoA Synthetase Long Chain Family Member 5 (ACSL5) in PDAC, its impact on fatty acid metabolism, and its clinical relevance. Through RNA sequencing, targeted metabolomics, proteomics, retrospective cohort studies, and a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments, the significance of ACSL5 was systematically investigated. Our results showed that ACSL5 was downregulated in GEM-resistant cells, and its high expression predicted better survival in PDAC patients. ACSL5 overexpression suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, and GEM resistance in PDAC cells, while its knockdown promoted these phenotypes. ACSL5 may exert its effects through the PPARδ/CPT1A signaling pathway, thereby influencing fatty acid β-oxidation. Notably, ACSL5 selectively modulated n-6 docosapentaenoic acid (DPA-n6) levels, while prospective cohort studies have shown that high plasma DPA-n6 is an independent risk factor for poor prognosis. Junction Plakoglobin (JUP) was identified as an ACSL5-binding protein and was associated with ACSL5 ubiquitination and protein stability. In summary, ACSL5 acts as a tumor suppressor in PDAC by modulating fatty acid metabolism. DPA-n6 may serve as a novel prognostic biomarker, highlighting the clinical relevance of ACSL5-associated lipid metabolism in PDAC.

items.title: Phase I dose-escalation study of stereotactic body radiotherapy with elective nodal irradiation for borderline resectable and unresectable locally advanced pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Locoregional recurrence remains a major clinical challenge in borderline resectable (BR) and unresectable locally advanced (UR-LA) pancreatic cancer, even after stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT). This phase I trial evaluated the safety, maximum tolerated dose (MTD), and preliminary efficacy of adding prophylactic elective nodal irradiation (ENI) to 5-fraction SBRT.
METHODS: Patients with BR/UR-LAPC were enrolled in a 3 + 3 dose-escalation design. SBRT was delivered in 5 fractions using either adaptive magnetic resonance image-guided radiation therapy or respiratory breath-hold radiotherapy with a fiducial marker. The ENI dose was fixed at 30 Gy in five fractions, while the primary tumor dose increased from Level 1 (35 Gy) to Level 3 (40 Gy). The primary endpoint was acute dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) (any Grade ≥ 3 non-hematological adverse events within 14 days after the completion of SBRT).
RESULTS: Twelve patients (BR: 4, LA: 8) were enrolled, 11 of whom had previously received systemic chemotherapy. One patient at Level 1 experienced acute Grade 3 anorexia/nausea requiring hospitalization. No DLTs were observed at Levels 2 and 3, and the MTD was not reached. Three patients with preexisting biliary stents developed subacute Grade 3 cholangitis. No Grade ≥ 3 late adverse events occurred. The median overall survival after SBRT was 17.3 months, and the 1-year locoregional control rate was 75%.
CONCLUSION: Five-fraction SBRT with simultaneous 30 Gy ENI was feasible, and the MTD was not reached within the tested dose levels up to 40 Gy. Further prospective studies are needed to evaluate its long-term safety and treatment outcomes.

items.title: Targeting ELF3 with Biomimetic Nanotherapy Sensitizes PDAC to Gemcitabine via GSDME-mediated Pyroptosis.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) continues to be a lethal malignancy with limited effective treatment strategies due to modest intrinsic response to systemic chemotherapy. Moreover, the dense, fibrotic stroma and poor vasculature of pancreatic tumors severely restrict drug penetration and therapeutic efficacy. The transcription factor ELF3 acts as a key oncogenic driver that promotes tumor growth, metastasis, and chemoresistance. To address these delivery barriers and enhance therapeutic response, we developed a biomimetic nanoplatform using cancer cell membrane-coated ZIF-8 nanoparticles (CNPs) to co-deliver gemcitabine (GEM) and an ELF3-targeting shRNA (shELF3), aiming to improve tumor-targeting specificity and elucidate the underlying cell death mechanism. Efficient encapsulation of GEM and shRNA ELF3 within a biomimetic nanocarrier was successfully confirmed. In vitro evaluation demonstrated that GEM/shELF3-CNPs activated canonical caspase-3/gasdermin E (GSDME)-dependent pyroptosis, resulting in markedly enhanced cytotoxicity in 6606 PDA cells. Furthermore, in vivo administration yielded superior tumor accumulation, potent tumor growth suppression, and significantly prolonged survival in the murine PDAC model, alongside favorable biosafety profiles. Our findings demonstrate that combining ELF3 silencing with gemcitabine delivery via biomimetic nanocarriers presents a promising synergistic strategy to sensitize pancreatic tumors and enhance PDAC therapeutic outcomes. The graphical representation of the study is shown in Fig. 1.

items.title: Cellularity Improvement of EUS-FNB Specimens for Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma Using a Cell-Capturing Scaffold.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Molecular profiling is increasingly relevant in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), requiring endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle biopsy (EUS-FNB) specimens with adequate tumor cellularity for downstream genomic analyses. Conventional specimen processing methods may be limited by suboptimal cellularity and blood contamination. A cell-capturing scaffold (CCS), a foam-like porous structure designed to retain cytological material, may improve specimen quality and cellular yield. This study aimed to compare histologic adequacy and neoplastic cellularity between CCS-processed and conventional formalin-fixed (FM) EUS-FNB specimens. Methods: Consecutive patients who underwent EUS-guided tissue acquisition for solid pancreatic lesions between November 2023 and June 2024 were retrospectively included. Tissue acquisition was performed using a 22-gauge Franseen-tip FNB needle. The first needle pass was processed using CCS, while subsequent passes were dispersed in formalin. Histologic adequacy, microfragment length and neoplastic cellularity were assessed by two expert pancreatic pathologists using dedicated scoring systems. Results: Twenty patients were included, with diagnoses of PDAC. Histologic core material was obtained in 17 CCS-processed and 15 FM samples, with no significant difference in histologic adequacy or microfragment length between groups (p = 0.414 and p = 0.276, respectively). CCS-processed samples showed a trend toward higher neoplastic cellularity compared with FM specimens (p = 0.0506). Conclusions: In this retrospective pilot study, CCS processing was associated with a trend toward higher neoplastic cellularity in EUS-FNB specimens from patients with PDAC, with comparable histologic adequacy. Further prospective studies are warranted to confirm these results and to evaluate the potential role of CCS in molecular analyses of pancreatic EUS-FNB specimens.

items.title: Schisandrin B Suppresses Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Through EGFR/AKT/mTOR Signaling and Mitochondrial Dysfunction.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal cancer with poor prognosis due to chemoresistance and limited treatment options. Schisandrin B (Sch B), a bioactive compound from Schisandra chinensis, has demonstrated anticancer effects in various malignancies, but its role in PDAC remains unknown. This study explores the antitumor mechanisms of Sch B using network pharmacology, molecular docking, and in vitro and in vivo experiments, focusing on the EGFR/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway and mitochondrial dysfunction. Network pharmacology identified EGFR, CASP3, BCL2, and HSP90 as key candidate targets of Sch B, and molecular docking and MD simulation were used to explore putative interactions with these proteins. In PDAC cells, treatment Sch B for 48 h reduced cell viability. In addition, Sch B suppressed EGFR/AKT/mTOR signaling and induced mitochondrial dysfunction, characterized by loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, increased mitochondrial and cytosolic calcium levels, and elevated ROS production, accompanied by activation of apoptotic signaling. Co-treatment with gemcitabine demonstrated enhanced effects, elevating apoptosis and oxidative stress. Moreover, Sch B significantly reduced tumor growth in a PANC-1 xenograft model, accompanied by decreased protein expression of EGFR, AKT, mTOR, and HSP90 in tumor tissues. These findings suggest that Sch B exerts antitumor activity associated with modulation of EGFR/AKT/mTOR signaling and mitochondrial dysfunction, supporting further investigation of Sch B as a potential therapeutic candidate for PDAC, particularly in combination with standard chemotherapy.

items.title: Changing Course: Semaphorins and Plexins as Novel Therapeutic Opportunities and Key Regulators of Pancreatic Cancer Microenvironment.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the deadliest solid tumors, and despite recent advances in surgical and systemic therapies, outcomes remain poor, rooted as much in the genetic mutations that initiate the disease as in a fibrotic, poorly vascularized microenvironment marked by scarce immune infiltration and a dense network of nerve fibers. Semaphorins, together with their receptors plexins and co-receptors neuropilins, have emerged as pivotal orchestrators of this microenvironment, shaping crosstalk between malignant cells, fibroblasts, macrophages, the endothelium, and peripheral neurons. This review examines how individual semaphorin family members drive, or in select contexts restrain, stromal activation, immune exclusion, pathological angiogenesis and neural remodeling. Building on this mechanistic framework, we explore the clinical relevance that semaphorin-mediated signaling holds for PDAC, from its potential as a prognostic and predictive biomarker to its growing promise as a therapeutic target, positioning this axis as a compelling frontier for improving outcomes in a disease that has long resisted meaningful therapeutic advances.

items.title: Pancreatic SBRT in Italian Clinical Practice: A Multicenter Analysis of 473 Patients Treated in 17 Centers.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma remains one of the most lethal malignancies, with limited options for durable local control. Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) has emerged as a promising modality, particularly with the advent of MR-guided radiotherapy (MRgRT) and the possibility of delivering ablative dose levels. This multicenter study aimed to describe real-world Italian practice, evaluate safety and outcomes, and assess the association between ablative dosing, MRgRT, radiological response, and local control.
METHODS: A retrospective multicenter analysis was conducted across 17 Italian centers, including 473 patients treated with SBRT between 2021 and 2025. Clinical, dosimetric, toxicity, and outcome data were collected. BED10 was calculated for all treatments. Radiological response was assessed using RECIST 1.1 criteria, and toxicity was graded according to CTCAE v5.0. Survival outcomes were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.
RESULTS: Median age was 69.6 years, and 59.4% of patients had ECOG performance status 0-1. The study population consisted predominantly of patients with non-metastatic disease, including resectable, borderline resectable, and unresectable locally advanced pancreatic cancer. Most patients received pre-SBRT chemotherapy (78%). The most common regimen was 45 Gy in 5 fractions. MRgRT was used in 20% of cases and was associated with reduced treatment margins (3-5 mm) and improved duodenal sparing (V33 < 0.5 cc in 91%). Acute grade ≥ 3 toxicity was 3.7%, and Late toxicity was uncommon, with grade ≥ 3 events observed in 3.0% of evaluable patients. Radiological response showed complete response in 5%, partial response in 27.7%, stable disease in 44.3%, and progressive disease in 23%, corresponding to an overall disease control rate of 77%. Patients receiving BED10 ≥ 80 Gy achieved higher partial response rates (38% vs. 19%) and lower progression rates (12% vs. 23%) compared with those receiving BED10 < 80 Gy. Median overall survival was 18.4 months, and median progression-free survival (PFS) was 10.2 months.
CONCLUSIONS: SBRT demonstrated a favorable safety profile and was associated with encouraging clinical outcomes in real-world Italian practice. Ablative dose delivery (BED10 ≥ 80 Gy) was associated with improved radiological response and local control without an apparent increase in toxicity. MRgRT was associated with improved organ-at-risk protection and may facilitate the safe delivery of ablative dose levels. The present findings primarily reflect outcomes in a predominantly non-metastatic population and support the role of SBRT as a component of modern multidisciplinary pancreatic cancer management. This pooled national analysis may serve as the basis for future prospective studies aimed at optimizing patient selection, dose prescription, and image-guided treatment strategies.

items.title: Circulating Tumor DNA Across the Patient Journey in Pancreatic Cancer: From Molecular Profiling to Dynamic Disease Monitoring.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) provides molecular information at different stages of the pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patient journey, but its clinical value differs according to when and why it is measured. This narrative review examines ctDNA from diagnosis and molecular profiling through neoadjuvant therapy, postoperative molecular residual disease (MRD), surveillance, and dynamic monitoring during systemic therapy, critically assessing the strength and limitations of the evidence at each clinical stage and its implications for clinical decision-making.
METHODS: Relevant studies were identified primarily through PubMed/MEDLINE, supplemented by forward citation tracking in Google Scholar, backward reference screening, and ClinicalTrials.gov searches for ongoing interventional studies. Original PDAC clinical studies were prioritized, with selected reviews, guidelines, consensus statements, and position papers used for context.
RESULTS: In localized disease, limited ctDNA shedding constrains diagnostic sensitivity, although baseline detection may provide prognostic information. After surgery, ctDNA positivity consistently identifies patients at increased risk of recurrence, whereas a negative result cannot reliably exclude residual disease. During surveillance, newly detectable or rising ctDNA may precede radiological recurrence. In advanced disease, serial ctDNA kinetics provide increasingly consistent information on treatment response and progression. Evidence for dynamic monitoring is increasing, but evidence that ctDNA-guided treatment or surveillance improves patient outcomes remains insufficient.
CONCLUSIONS: The clinical value of ctDNA depends on when and why it is measured. ctDNA should complement rather than replace conventional assessments. By distinguishing established prognostic associations from emerging monitoring applications and unproven ctDNA-guided interventions, this review provides a practical framework for interpreting ctDNA across the PDAC patient journey. Prospective trials are needed to determine whether ctDNA-guided decisions improve patient outcomes.

items.title: Hydrophobic ion pairing enabled self-nanoemulsifying niclosamide for pancreatic cancer: improved drug loading and kinetic solubility.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is an aggressive and relatively uncommon disease characterized by profound dense fibrosis and late-stage diagnosis. An anthelmintic drug, Niclosamide (NIC), has been widely repurposed as an anticancer agent, but its poor aqueous solubility resulted in < 10 % oral bioavailability, while its poor lipid solubility poses substantial challenges for the development of a translational oral formulation. Herein, we have developed a self-nanoemulsifying (SNEDDS) formulation (NanoNic) that utilizes Transcutol® P as cosolvent and leverages the Hydrophobic Ion-Pairing (HIP) complexation strategy to improve drug loading and stability. To this end, we screened cationic complexing agents with different amine functionalities - primary, ternary and quaternary. Cationic ionizable lipid/DLin-DMA was selected as pairing agent based on its superior biocompatibility, complexation efficiency, and kinetic stability. Incorporation of cationic ionizable lipid forming a hydrophobic complex with NIC resulted in nearly 30 % reduction in globule size to ∼ 67 nm with a zeta potential >+35 mV. Optimized NanoNic (HIP-loaded SNEDDS) demonstrated ∼ 4-fold higher drug-loading compared to traditional SNEDDS (without a complexing agent), which showed immediate drug precipitation after redispersion. HIP-loaded NanoNic preconcentrate was stable for over 3 months, whereas its aqueous dispersion exhibited only 2 % drug precipitation within 24 h. The Quality-by-Design approach was employed to optimize the nano-globule size of the formulation/NanoNic. Furthermore, NanoNic displayed significant anti-angiogenic activity (HUVEC model) and anticancer efficacy in 2D and 3D models of naïve and gemcitabine-resistant MiaPaCa-2 spheroids. Thus, collective use of Transcutol®P and Ionizable lipid enabled self-nanoemulsifying system with high drug load, reduced globule size and high kinetic solubility.

items.title: Pulmonary metastasectomy for isolated pulmonary metastases from pancreatic cancer: Patient selection and outcomes in a single-center retrospective cohort.
items.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pulmonary metastases from pancreatic cancer tend to occur later than other patterns of disease recurrence. The role of pulmonary metastasectomy remains unclear, particularly regarding patient selection and the influence of underlying tumor biology. This study aimed to explore factors that may reflect underlying tumor biology by evaluating the oncological outcomes of patients with isolated pulmonary metastases from pancreatic cancer who underwent pulmonary metastasectomy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients who underwent complete resection of initial pulmonary metastases following curative surgery for pancreatic cancer between 2012 and 2022 were retrospectively examined. Survival outcomes after pulmonary metastasectomy and potential prognostic factors were evaluated.
RESULTS: Eighteen patients who underwent complete resection of pulmonary metastases from pancreatic cancer were included in the analysis. The median disease-free interval was 35 months (range, 11-66 months). Solitary pulmonary metastasis was observed in 14 patients, while two pulmonary metastases were observed in 4 patients. The median follow-up period censored after pulmonary metastasectomy was 51.5 months (range, 9-127). The 3-year recurrence-free survival (RFS) rate was 63.4%, and the 3-year overall survival rate was 91.7%. Patients without lymph node metastasis from primary pancreatic cancer had a significantly higher 3-year RFS (88.9%) than those with lymph node metastasis (35.6%, p = 0.043).
CONCLUSION: Favorable recurrence and survival outcomes were observed in patients with isolated pulmonary metastases after primary pancreatic cancer surgery who were carefully selected based on features suggestive of indolent tumor biology. Lymph node status of the primary pancreatic cancer may help identify patients with more favorable tumor biology who may achieve better disease control after pulmonary metastasectomy.

ELF3 (E74 like ETS transcription factor 3) promotes tumor growth and autophagy in pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the research progress of the past decades, the prognosis for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma remains poor. Identifying novel targets and exploring the underlying mechanisms is therefore of great importance. ELF3 (E74 like ETS transcription factor 3) is a member of the E-twenty-six (ETS) family and previous studies suggest that ELF3 may play a promoting role in malignant epithelial tumor; however, the effect and exact mechanism have not been determined in pancreatic cancer.
METHODS: ELF3 expression and its prognostic relevance in pancreatic cancer were analyzed using clinical datasets. The role of ELF3 in autophagy regulation was evaluated using molecular and cellular approaches in vitro and in vivo. Computer-aided drug design was performed to identify potential ELF3 inhibitors, whose anti-tumor efficacy was subsequently evaluated.
RESULTS: In the present study, it is observed that high expression of ELF3 leads to a poor overall survival in pancreatic cancer patients. Functional experiments demonstrated that knockdown of ELF3 blocks autophagy. In addition, SRT2183 was identified as a potential ELF3 inhibitor using molecular docking. In vitro and in vivo results showed that SRT2183 blocks autophagy and exerts anti-carcinoma effect.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that ELF3 promotes autophagy through transcriptional regulation of ATG10 and identify ELF3 as a potential therapeutic target in pancreatic cancer. SRT2183, an ELF3-targeting compound that suppresses autophagic flux and tumor growth, represents a promising candidate for further therapeutic development.

items.title: A Spatial Multi-omics Atlas of Intra- and Extrapancreatic Perineural Invasion Reveals Basal-like Neurotropism and Stromal Remodeling in Pancreatic Cancer.
items.abstract: Perineural invasion (PNI) is a prominent feature of pancreatic cancer (PDAC) and is closely associated with tumor progression and poor prognosis. However, its spatial cellular architecture and underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we applied high-resolution spatial transcriptomics to construct a comprehensive atlas of the PNI microenvironment across distinct anatomical regions of intra and extra-pancreas. We observed that the Basal-like tumor subtype exhibited a higher propensity for PNI compared with the Classical subtype, a finding further supported by multiplex imaging on whole-mount histopathology. Comparative spatial analysis revealed distinct immune and stromal organization between tumor subtypes, with enrichment of M2-like macrophage potentially promoting epithelial cell migration in the vicinity of Basal-like tumors. In addition, we identified myofibroblast subset may promote Schwann cell activation and PNI-associated nerve injury was further accompanied by a shift toward inflammatory fibroblast polarization and features of CD8+ T cell exhaustion within the local microenvironment. Finally, spatial profiling indicated functional heterogeneity among tumor-associated Schwann cells, which may contribute to the tumor progression. Collectively, this study provides a spatially resolved view of the cellular and molecular landscape of PNI in PDAC and offers insights into Basal-specific neurotropic behavior and microenvironmental reorganization.

items.title: PDAC: Efficient coreset selection for continual learning via probability density awareness.
items.abstract: Rehearsal-based Continual Learning (CL) maintains a limited buffer to store replay samples for knowledge retention, making them heavily reliant on sample quality. Current methods typically construct the buffer by selecting a representative coreset, aiming to approximate the training efficacy of the full dataset with minimal storage overhead. However, mainstream Coreset Selection (CS) methods generally construct coresets via computationally expensive bi-level optimization, limiting their efficiency. In this paper, we provide an efficient selection logic and scheme for coreset construction, avoiding computationally expensive bi-level optimization. By decomposing the mean squared error between the buffer-trained and Bayes-optimal models, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate that high-density samples are primary contributors to variance suppression. Inspired by this, we propose the Probability Density-Aware Coreset (PDAC) method, utilizing a Projected Gaussian Mixture (PGM) model to achieve efficient density-prioritized selection. To further handle streaming scenarios, we incorporate a streaming expectation maximization algorithm to develop Streaming PDAC (SPDAC). Experiments show our methods outperforms other baselines across various CL settings while ensuring favorable efficiency.

items.title: Histopathological findings associated with prognosis in resected ductal adenocarcinoma of the pancreas.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ductal adenocarcinoma of the pancreas is among the most lethal neoplasms of the digestive tract. It is frequently diagnosed at advanced stages and associated with limited overall survival, even after surgical resection with curative intent. Although pathological staging is fundamental for prognostic stratification, patients with similar anatomical stages may have distinct clinical outcomes, suggesting that additional histopathological factors influence disease evolution.
AIMS: This study aimed to assess the prognostic impact of histopathological variables on the overall survival of patients with ductal adenocarcinoma of the pancreas who underwent surgical resection, with emphasis on lymph node involvement and angiolymphatic invasion.
METHODS: This observational, retrospective study included patients who underwent surgical resection for ductal adenocarcinoma of the pancreas at a tertiary hospital between 2017 and 2024. Clinical, anatomopathological, and therapeutic data were obtained by reviewing medical records and histopathological reports. Overall survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and prognostic factors were analyzed using univariate and multivariate Cox regression models.
RESULTS: A total of 58 patients were included. Lymph node metastases were identified in approximately half of the cases, and angiolymphatic invasion was frequently observed. During follow-up, more than half of the patients died. The median overall survival was 19.63 months. In the univariate analysis, lymph node involvement, lymph node ratio, extranodal extension, and angiolymphatic invasion were associated with worse overall survival. In the multivariate analysis, lymph node status maintained an independent association with worse prognosis, with a progressive increase in risk according to nodal stage, as did angiolymphatic invasion.
CONCLUSIONS: Lymph node involvement and angiolymphatic invasion are independent prognostic factors associated with worse overall survival in resected ductal adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. Systematic evaluation of these histopathological variables can support better prognostic stratification, helping individualize postoperative treatment.
CENTRAL MESSAGE: Histopathological findings, particularly angiolymphatic invasion and lymph node involvement, are associated with reduced overall survival in resected ductal adenocarcinoma of the pancreas, reflecting the impact of tumor biology beyond traditional staging.
PERSPECTIVES: The systematic incorporation of qualitative histopathological variables, such as the presence of angiolymphatic invasion and characteristics of lymph node involvement, may improve prognostic stratification of patients with ductal adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. These variables can help identify higher-risk subgroups among patients with similar pathological stages, supporting follow-up and adjuvant treatment individualization. Further studies are needed to validate their application in clinical practice.

items.title: Social Deprivation, not Rurality, is Associated with Receipt of Guideline-concordant Care for Pancreatic Cancer in North Carolina, USA.
items.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Rural-dwelling patients with pancreatic cancer (PC) and a higher Social Deprivation Index (SDI) score may be less likely to receive guideline-concordant care (GCC) than patients living in urban areas. We hypothesized that SDI score and rurality would affect the receipt of GCC among patients with PC.
METHODS: The North Carolina Central Cancer Registry was queried to identify patients with PC from 2004 to 2019. GCC was defined by National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines for PC/Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results staging as localized disease (surgery/chemotherapy), regional disease (at least chemotherapy), or distant disease (chemotherapy and/or palliative care). Multivariable regression assessed the impact of patient-level factors, SDI score, and geographic location on the receipt of GCC.
RESULTS: The cohort included 3595 patients with PC: 2532 (70%) urban and 1063 (30%) rural dwellers. Most had regional disease at diagnosis (n = 1871; 52%), were aged 65-79 years (n = 2021; 56%), were female (n = 1891; 53%), were non-Hispanic white (n = 2619; 73%), and had a medium SDI score (n = 1767; 49%), a Charlson Comorbidity Index score of 0 (n = 987; 27.5%), and a Frailty Index of 3+ (n = 976; 27%). GCC was received by 151 (32%) patients with localized disease, 1533 (82%) with regional, and 886 (71%) with distant disease. Across all stages, high (odds ratio [OR] 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.55-0.92) and medium (OR 0.82; 95% CI 0.67-1.00) SDI scores were associated with a decreased likelihood of receiving GCC. Among localized patients, those with high (OR 0.43; 95% CI 0.21-0.85) and medium (OR 0.47; 95% CI 0.27-0.81) SDI scores had decreased GCC. There was no association between SDI score and GCC among patients with regionalized and distant disease. Across all stages, there was no association between GCC and geographic location.
CONCLUSION: Social deprivation, not rurality, was associated with a decreased receipt of GCC for patients with PC. Multilevel interventions are needed to modify barriers and facilitators of GCC receipt at a state level.

items.title: Foundation-model imaging biomarkers for pancreatic cancer: cross-species discovery of conserved tumour biology in mouse MRI and human CT.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computed tomography (CT) stages pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) but does not read out the treatment-guiding tumour biology, requiring biopsy. Whether an imaging-biology relationship discovered in preclinical MRI holds independently in human CT is unknown.
METHODS: One pipeline was applied to two PDAC cohorts: longitudinal 9.4 T multi-parametric MRI (169 sessions; 1002 image series, 471 quantitative maps) with terminal histopathology in male C57BL/6 mice bearing orthotopic KPC-derived tumours treated with gemcitabine, a dendritic-cell vaccine, both, or neither, and abdominal CT with matched proteogenomics from CPTAC-PDA. Radiomics and frozen foundation-model embeddings were modelled under grouped cross-validation against five pre-specified paired endpoints, with no cross-species transfer of features, weights, or labels.
FINDINGS: Applied independently, the pipeline recovered four matched molecular endpoints in both species (CD8 infiltration, stromal collagen, CD8:CD68 immune balance, cytolytic activity), with areas under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUROCs) of 0.938-0.960 in mice and 0.780-0.856 in humans. Survival concordance indices were 0.729 and 0.689. After adjustment for age, stage, and grade, the human imaging score remained independently prognostic (hazard ratio 1.87 per SD, 95% CI 1.32 to 2.66; p < 0.001 [Wald test]; combined concordance index 0.726 versus 0.611 for clinical covariates). Findings held in portal-venous-restricted analysis; frozen embeddings outperformed end-to-end fine-tuning in both arms.
INTERPRETATION: One pipeline recovered matched PDAC biology in mouse MRI and human CT, supporting preclinical imaging to nominate non-invasive CT biomarker candidates for biopsy-sparing PDAC trial stratification, pending prospective external validation.
FUNDING: National Cancer Institute; Society of Interventional Radiology Foundation; University of California Irvine Anticancer Challenge Pilot grant.

items.title: Albumin-bound paclitaxel-induced stromal reprogramming drives resistance to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal malignancy for which neoadjuvant chemotherapy with albumin-bound paclitaxel combined with gemcitabine (AG) is a standard first-line approach for borderline resectable and locally advanced disease. However, secondary resistance to this regimen is common, and its underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. In this study, we investigated how neoadjuvant AG therapy shapes the tumor stroma in PDAC. Single-cell transcriptomics of patient tumors revealed that AG treatment induces a phenotypic switch of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) from myofibroblastic (myCAF) to inflammatory (iCAF) states and identified a previously unrecognized TMEM100+CAF subset enriched in nonresponders. Mechanistic studies showed that albumin-bound paclitaxel activates IL-2-STAT5 signaling to drive TMEM100 expression and that TMEM100+CAFs promote chemoresistance through paracrine secretion of amphiregulin (AREG) and activation of tumor EGFR signaling. Genetic ablation of TMEM100+CAFs in mouse models reversed CAF switching and enhanced the antitumor efficacy of AG therapy. These findings map chemotherapy-induced CAF plasticity, reveal a TMEM100-AREG axis of resistance, and highlight TMEM100+CAFs as a promising target to sensitize PDAC to neoadjuvant treatment.

items.title: A TROP2-targeting aptamer enables selective drug delivery and potent antitumor activity in pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains difficult to treat, highlighting the need for strategies that selectively deliver cytotoxic agents to tumor cells. Trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (TROP2) has been proposed as a candidate therapeutic target in PDAC, but non-antibody-based delivery formats remain underexplored. Using protein-SELEX, we identified T17, a high-affinity aptamer that specifically binds to TROP2, and conjugated it to monomethyl auristatin E through an MC-Val-Cit-PAB linker to generate the aptamer-drug conjugate T17-M. Preclinical evaluation in cellular and animal models showed that T17-M retained TROP2-dependent binding, underwent clathrin-mediated internalization and lysosomal processing, and suppressed tumor growth in cell-line-derived and patient-derived xenografts. T17-M also reduced liver metastasis and induced calreticulin exposure, ATP release, and HMGB1 secretion, consistent with immunogenic cell death. In immunocompetent models, T17-M promoted dendritic-cell activation and CD8+ T cell infiltration, while its combination with PD-1 blockade further enhanced tumor control and prolonged survival. These findings provide preclinical proof-of-concept for T17-M as an alternative TROP2-targeted drug-delivery strategy for PDAC.

items.title: Hepatocyte Serine Fuels Pancreatic Cancer Liver Metastasis.
Tumor microenvironment-driven therapeutic resistance in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most treatment-refractory malignancies, with limited and often transient benefit from chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and radiotherapy. Therapeutic resistance is increasingly recognized as an ecosystem-level process arising from reciprocal interactions between malignant cells and the tumor microenvironment (TME). Dense extracellular matrix, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), pancreatic stellate cells (PSCs), dysfunctional vasculature, immunosuppressive myeloid and lymphoid populations, hypoxic niches, metabolic networks, microbiota, extracellular vesicles (EVs), and neural components collectively restrict drug delivery and promote adaptive survival, immune escape, stemness, and treatment-induced evolution. This review integrates these processes into a PDAC resistance ecosystem framework. We discuss how stromal remodeling, hypoxia-driven adaptation, metabolic-immune crosstalk, extracellular communication, cancer stem cell plasticity, and TME-regulated autophagy and ferroptosis contribute to resistance across therapeutic modalities. We further evaluate emerging strategies involving stromal reprogramming, myeloid and immune remodeling, metabolic intervention, hypoxia targeting, and regulated cell-death sensitization. Particular emphasis is placed on the limited clinical translation of indiscriminate stromal depletion and single-target approaches. Finally, we propose that spatial multi-omics, longitudinal biomarker profiling, and adaptive combination therapy will be required to identify dominant resistance programs and guide patient-specific intervention in PDAC.

items.title: Serum extracellular vesicle proteomics reveals treatment-associated biomarkers in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
items.abstract:
Background

Longitudinal biomarkers of treatment response in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) are needed. Extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched serum proteomics may provide a minimally invasive approach for monitoring systemic and tumor-associated responses to therapy.

Methods

Paired pre-treatment and post-treatment serum samples were analyzed from 51 patients with pancreatic cancer, including 25 treated with FOLFIRINOX and 20 treated with gemcitabine-based therapy. EVs were enriched using the Mag-Net method and profiled by data independent acquisition mass spectrometry. After batch correction and filtering, 941 proteins were retained for differential and pathway analyses. Paired linear models and gene set enrichment analyses were used to assess treatment-associated changes. Baseline protein abundance and longitudinal changes were evaluated in relation to overall survival (OS) using Cox models.

Results

A total of 2,089 EV-associated proteins were identified, with an average of 1,186 proteins quantified per sample. Across the cohort, 26 proteins differed between post- and pretreatment samples. Proteins that increased after treatment were primarily related to extracellular matrix organization and cell adhesion, whereas proteins that decreased after treatment were associated with actin cytoskeletal organization, coagulation, and hemostasis. Treatment-associated changes were more pronounced in the FOLFIRINOX group, in which 32 proteins were differentially expressed. FOLFIRINOX was characterized by coordinated reductions in platelet- and coagulation-associated proteins, including PF4, PF4V1, PPBP, GP5, ITGA2B, and ITGB3, accompanied by enrichment of platelet activation, coagulation, and hemostasis pathways among down-regulated processes. No individual proteins met the same significance threshold in the gemcitabine group. A composite seven-protein platelet score decreased significantly after FOLFIRINOX but not for gemcitabine, and the between-regimen difference in score change was significant. Higher pretreatment ITGB1 abundance was associated with longer OS after multiple-testing correction (HR, 0.112; BH-FDR = 0.0063). In multivariable analysis, greater treatment-associated platelet-score depletion was independently associated with shorter OS (HR per unit increase in Δscore, 0.56; P = 0.030).

Conclusions

Longitudinal serum EV-enriched proteomics identified treatment-associated biological changes in PDAC, including a coordinated platelet-related response predominantly observed after FOLFIRINOX. Baseline ITGB1 abundance and longitudinal platelet-score changes represent potentially complementary prognostic and pharmacodynamic markers. These findings are exploratory and require validation in larger, independent cohorts incorporating platelet counts, coagulation measurements, and targeted proteomic assays.
