items.title: Dual-Loaded Curcumin-Metformin Niosomes: Physicochemical Characterization and In Vitro Activity in Colorectal and Pancreatic Cancer Cells.
items.abstract:
PURPOSE: Colorectal cancer and pancreatic cancer represent some of the most aggressive forms of cancer. Curcumin (CUR) and Metformin (MET) have distinct pharmacokinetic profiles. MET is water-soluble, whereas CUR is highly lipophilic. These differences in their kinetic behavior may limit their synchronized therapeutic activity when used in combination. This study aimed to develop and characterize dual-loaded curcumin-MET niosomes (NIO-CUR-MET) and evaluate their physicochemical properties, drug release behavior, and in vitro anticancer, apoptotic, and anti-inflammatory effects against HCT-116 (colorectal) and PANC-1 (pancreatic) cancer cell lines.
METHODS: Niosomes were prepared using the ethanol injection method and characterized using dynamic light scattering. Drug loading efficiency was determined by HPLC. Drug release was assessed over 72 hours using a dialysis method at 37°C. Anticancer activity was evaluated using the MTT assay, apoptosis via Caspase-3/7 analysis, and anti-inflammatory effects by measuring TNF-α and IL-1β levels using ELISA.
RESULTS: The particle size of 152.7±54 nm, and zeta potential of -12±1.3 mV, indicating a stable and uniform nanosystem. Encapsulation efficiencies were achieved for MET (91.5%±5%) and CUR (39.8%±7%). Release was observed ~95% for CURand ~92% for MET over 72 hours. The NIO-CUR-MET formulation significantly enhanced cytotoxicity compared to free and single-drug forms, with lower IC₅₀ values in HCT-116 (4±3.2 µM for CUR and 190±10.2 µM for MET) and PANC-1 cells IC₅₀ values (5.2±0.9 µM for CUR and 202.5±8.2 µM for MET). It also induced a 5.3-fold increase in apoptosis (P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Dual-loaded niosomes improved drug delivery performance and exhibited enhanced therapeutic efficacy against target cancer cell lines.

items.title: Developing a Multimodal miR-15a Mimic to Overcome Gemcitabine and RAS(ON) Inhibitor Daraxonrasib Resistance in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
items.abstract: Gemcitabine remains a mainstay of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) treatment, while the RAS(ON) inhibitor daraxonrasib has recently demonstrated improved survival in previously treated metastatic disease. However, acquired resistance to both therapies remains a major clinical challenge. Here, we developed MTX-5-FU-Gem-miR-15a, a multimodal microRNA (miRNA)-based therapeutic, by chemically modifying tumor-suppressive miR-15a with methotrexate (MTX), 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), and gemcitabine (Gem) to combine sequence specific gene regulation with disruption of nucleotide metabolism. MTX-5-FU-Gem-miR-15a exhibited low-nanomolar potency across five PDAC cell lines and retained activity in gemcitabine- and daraxonrasib-resistant models under vehicle-free conditions, substantially exceeding that of stoichiometrically matched free antimetabolites. Treatment induced S-phase accumulation, increased DNA damage and apoptosis, and suppressed checkpoint and survival-associated proteins, including WEE1, CHK1, YAP1, and BCL-2. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed increased DNA replication, replication-stress, and repair-associated programs, together with reduced oncogenic signaling. In gemcitabine-resistant cells, treatment restored the gemcitabine-activating enzyme dCK, reduced ABCC1 and ABCC3 expression, and suppressed resistance-associated signaling programs, indicating partial remodeling of resistance-associated pathways. MTX-5-FU-Gem-miR-15a also synergized with daraxonrasib (mean Bliss synergy score, 22.52) and activated tumor-cell-intrinsic STING-TBK1 signaling, accompanied by increased interferon stimulated gene expression and IFN-β and CXCL10 secretion. Finally, MTX-5-FU-Gem-miR-15a retained low-nanomolar potency in three patient-derived PDAC organoids and significantly suppressed metastatic tumor growth  in vivo at 4 mg/kg. Together, these findings support a multimodal miRNA therapeutic strategy that combines replication-associated DNA damage, checkpoint protein suppression, and innate immune activation-associated responses to target therapeutic resistance in PDAC.

items.title: Effective Targeting of p53-Mutant Colorectal and Pancreatic Cancers by Combinatorial Therapeutic Strategy.
items.abstract: Existing treatment options for colorectal and pancreatic cancers harboring mutant p53 (p53mut) are largely ineffective and lack selectivity. Our novel therapeutic strategy for p53mut cancers with a thymidine analogue (TAS102) and a PARP inhibitor (PARPi) showed promising efficacy in a clinical trial, although the mechanisms remain not fully understood. Here, we investigated the molecular mechanisms underlying therapeutic efficacy of our approach and explored new combinations to further enhance the response. To define the contribution of each drug into the therapeutic response, we conducted an unbiased transcriptomic analysis in p53-proficient and p53mut cancer models. The biological effects were investigated in comprehensive analyses of cell proliferation, cell death, and DNA damage. The drug interactions were explored in cytotoxicity assays and efficacy was tested in patient-derived colorectal and pancreatic cancer models. We found that TAS102-PARPi treatment induces DNA breaks and long G2-arrest in p53mut cells, whereas normal cells rapidly repair their DNA and re-enter the cell cycle. Transcriptomic analysis showed that TAS102 is the major driver of the response, whereas PARPi improves selectivity of the TAS102 effects. The treatment does not block replication in p53mut cells but induces post-replicative DNA repair and represses mitosis. Delayed blockade of G2-checkpoint results in massive cell death in p53mut cells selectively. Priming TAS102-PARPi treatment in combination with delayed G2-checkpoint blockade was highly effective against cancer models and was well-tolerated in mice. Broadly, a novel two-step therapeutic strategy showed high efficacy and selectivity for p53mut cancers and low toxicity to normal tissues, demonstrating potential for clinical translation.

items.title: PancreaGuide for Computed Tomography Report Interpretation and Perioperative Consultation in Pancreatic Cancer: Development and Retrospective Evaluation of a Knowledge-Augmented Large Language Model Agent.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate interpretation of pancreatic cancer status and resectability-related information, together with effective perioperative communication, remains a major challenge in pancreatic cancer care. In routine practice, unstructured computed tomography (CT) reports and complex clinical information may limit the accessibility and consistency of clinical information delivery and increase the communication burden on clinicians. Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities for clinical information support; however, existing applications are often task-specific and rarely combine CT report interpretation with perioperative consultation within a unified patient-oriented framework.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and retrospectively evaluate PancreaGuide, a knowledge-augmented LLM agent designed to support clinician-supervised CT report-based interpretation of pancreatic cancer resectability-related information and standardized perioperative consultation.
METHODS: We developed PancreaGuide, an agent-based framework integrating structured prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, and a domain-specific pancreatic surgery knowledge base to support clinical information interpretation and perioperative consultation. A retrospective cohort of 444 patients who underwent contrast-enhanced CT at West China Hospital between 2023 and 2025 was analyzed. Three LLMs, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Gemini, were evaluated in both base and PancreaGuide-integrated configurations. CT report-based interpretation of resectability-related information was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic curves (ROCs), and decision curve analysis (DCA) using a surgery-based proxy reference. Perioperative consultation quality was evaluated across 5 dimensions: accuracy, completeness, consistency, safety, and robustness.
RESULTS: Higher classification metric point estimates were observed after integration of the PancreaGuide framework across all 3 backbone models. In CT report-based interpretation of resectability-related information, Gemini+ achieved the highest accuracy of 87.4% (95% CI 0.840-0.902) and a sensitivity of 95.9% (95% CI 0.927-0.978). All models showed improved sensitivity and specificity estimates after PancreaGuide integration, with improved agreement between model-generated interpretations and observed surgical management status. ROC and DCA suggested improved discrimination and estimated net benefit using the surgery-based proxy reference. In perioperative consultation, PancreaGuide-integrated models received higher expert-rated scores than their corresponding base models across all 5 evaluation dimensions. Gemini+ achieved the highest overall score (mean 3.88, SD 0.38), followed by ChatGPT+ (mean 3.8, SD 10.36) and DeepSeek+ (mean 3.75, SD 0.35). The greatest improvements were observed in completeness and robustness, with consistent gains across clinical consultation domains.
CONCLUSIONS: PancreaGuide provides a unified, knowledge-augmented framework for clinician-supervised CT report-based interpretation of resectability-related information and perioperative information support across multiple LLM backbones. The CT-based findings should be interpreted as agreement with observed surgical management status rather than validation against an independently adjudicated anatomical resectability. PancreaGuide may serve as an auxiliary information interpretation framework to improve the accessibility and consistency of clinical information delivery, while it should not replace formal radiological assessment, multidisciplinary evaluation, or clinician judgment.

items.title: Mutant KRAS vaccination for pancreatic cancer interception: the G12D immunogenicity paradox.
Complement C1q drives skeletal muscle wasting in pancreatic cancer
items.abstract: Cancer cachexia, defined by involuntary skeletal muscle loss, affects ~ 70% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients at diagnosis and independently worsens survival. Here, we identify complement component 1q (C1q) as a driver of PDAC-induced muscle wasting, with coordinated effects across muscle, tumor, and systemic inflammatory compartments. In cachectic PDAC patient muscle, C1q partially co-deposits with IgM, and C1q mRNA correlates with reduced muscle radiation attenuation, a CT-derived measure of muscle quality. In PDAC tumors, C1q protein correlates with immunosuppressive programs and independently predicts poor survival. These findings are recapitulated in orthotopic KPC mice, where C1q mRNA is upregulated in respiratory muscle before cachexia onset, and C1q deposits in tumors and co-deposits with IgM in muscles of cachectic mice. C1qa deletion reduced systemic inflammatory mediators, blocked muscle atrophy, and improved activity and grip strength in KPC mice, while attenuating immune cell infiltration and extracellular matrix remodeling in respiratory muscle. Host C1qa deletion also suppressed angiogenic and immunosuppressive programs in KPC tumors, while increasing intratumoral CD8⁺ T cell density and Granzyme B production. These findings position C1q as a driver of cancer-induced muscle wasting and tumor immunosuppression, supporting C1q inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy targeting pathological features of poor-prognosis PDAC.

items.title: GPR87 activates the NF-κB signal in LUAD cells to promote M2 polarization of macrophages.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), the predominant subtype of lung cancer, has limited therapeutic options. Dysregulation of the NF‑κB pathway and M2‑type polarization of macrophages (Macs) drive LUAD progression. GPR87, a member of the GPCR family, is overexpressed in multiple malignancies, including lung cancer, and has been demonstrated to activate NF-κB in pancreatic cancer. However, the function of GPR87 in LUAD and its role in microenvironment remodeling remain unclear.
METHODS: GPR87 levels in LUAD were analyzed by utilizing the TCGA database. The Kaplan-Meier was utilized for prognostic evaluation. The qPCR and WB were used to assess GPR87 levels in LUAD cell lines. A549 cell GPR87 overexpression model and NCI-H1975 cell GPR87 knockdown model were constructed, and through colony formation, CCK-8, flow cytometry and ELISA, the effects of GPR87 on cell progression, NF-κB signaling pathway and cytokine secretion were explored. A co-cultivation system of A549 cells and THP-1-derived Macs was employed to validate the regulatory effect of the GPR87/NF-κB axis on M2 polarization of Macs via flow cytometry, morphological observation, and ELISA, and validation was also performed using primary Macs derived from PBMCs. In addition, an syngeneic tumor model was established by utilizing C57BL/6 mice, and tumor proliferation, apoptosis, and protein expression were assessed through IHC and TUNEL staining.
RESULTS: TCGA-LUAD analysis showed that GPR87 was significantly upregulated in LUAD tissues, and GEPIA2 Kaplan-Meier analysis indicated that its high expression was associated with poor overall survival. qPCR and WB further validated the upregulation of GPR87 in LUAD cell lines. In A549 cells, overexpression of GPR87 enhanced colony formation ability and inhibited apoptosis, accompanied by activation of the NF-κB pathway, whereas knockdown of GPR87 produced opposite phenotypic effects. Mechanistic studies showed that the GPR87/NF-κB signaling axis induced THP-1-derived Macs to polarize toward the M2 phenotype, and this result was validated in primary Macs derived from PBMCs. In vivo experiments showed that GPR87 overexpression enhanced the tumorigenic ability of LLC cells, whereas this effect was significantly attenuated by the NF-κB inhibitor BAY 11-7082.
CONCLUSIONS: GPR87 promotes the malignant phenotype of LUAD cells and induces M2 polarization of Macs via activating the NF-κB signaling pathway. GPR87/NF-κB axis may serve as a novel therapeutic target for LUAD.

items.title: Targeting ferroptosis in major digestive system malignancies: regulatory networks and therapeutic opportunities.
items.abstract: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death that is associated with the accumulation of lipid peroxides, particularly in polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs)-containing cellular membranes. Ferroptosis is initiated by aberrant iron metabolism, intense reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, oxidative damage to membrane structures and disruption of the cystine/glutamate antiporter system (System Xc-)-glutathione (GSH)-glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) antioxidant pathway. Emerging evidence increasingly recognizes ferroptosis as a crucial mediator of tumor progression and response to therapy in digestive system malignancies. Aberrant iron homeostasis, lipid metabolic reprogramming, redox imbalance and remodeling of the tumor microenvironment (TME) are common events found in digestive system malignancies. This structured narrative review primarily focuses on colorectal cancer (CRC), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), gastric cancer (GC), and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) because ferroptosis regulatory mechanisms have been best defined for these cancers with respect to tumor-intrinsic regulation, metabolic vulnerability, antioxidant dependency, TME interactions and therapeutic responses. Additional evidence assessing whether the regulatory principles of ferroptosis extend to additional digestive system malignancies such as esophageal squamous-cell carcinoma and extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma is also presented. Collectively, these modifications contribute to ferroptosis sensitivity as well as tumor growth, treatment resistance and immune evasion. Ferroptosis is not simply regulated by a single linear pathway, but rather orchestrated through multilayered regulatory networks involving transcriptional and epigenetic control, metabolic rewiring, immune modulation, exosome-mediated communication and extensive crosstalk between numerous signaling pathways. The application of ferroptosis inducers, nano-platform delivery systems, TME-responsive methodology and multimodal combination schemes indicates emerging therapeutic approaches with potential translational implications for digestive system malignancies. Nonetheless, clinical translation is limited by mechanistic complexity, tumor heterogeneity, incompletely defined resistance mechanisms, uncertainty of reliable predictive biomarkers and unaddressed biosafety issues with nanoplatforms. Thus, this Review frames current evidence within a three-tier mechanistic-to-translational framework that connects a common iron-lipid-redox vulnerability axis possessing tumor-type-specific resistance programs and biomarker-directed therapeutic prioritization to delineate context-dependent ferroptosis vulnerabilities and priorities for future clinical evaluation.

items.title: Real-world characteristics, testing patterns, and outcomes in patients with tropomyosin receptor kinase fusion cancer from a large pooled clinicogenomic database.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tropomyosin receptor kinase (TRK) inhibitors are highly active in neurotrophic tyrosine receptor kinase (NTRK) gene fusion cancers. The registrational datasets of the three approved TRK inhibitors are well described in the literature but real-world data remain limited. To address this gap, we conducted the Real wOrld treAtment anD outcoMes Among Patients with TRK fusion cancer study.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This pooled analysis of five large, international clinicogenomic databases assessed patient characteristics, biomarker testing patterns, co-occurring genomic alterations, and clinical outcomes of patients with TRK fusion cancers.
RESULTS: A total of 451 patients with advanced/metastatic TRK fusion cancer were identified. NTRK gene fusions were mainly identified by next-generation sequencing [363 (81%) patients]. The median time from diagnosis of advanced/metastatic cancer to the date of the first NTRK gene fusion test was 25 days [interquartile range (IQR) 0-459]. Of the 172 (38%) patients who received a TRK inhibitor, the median time from NTRK gene fusion testing to first TRK inhibitor administration was 118 days (IQR 31-335). The median real-world overall survival was 28 months [95% confidence interval (CI) 21-32] for any first-line systemic therapy and it varied widely across tumor types, from 11 months (95% CI 8-17) for pancreatic cancer to 41 months (95% CI 25-50) for breast cancer.
CONCLUSIONS: This is the largest integrated real-world cohort describing patients with TRK fusion cancer to date, providing a comprehensive picture of TRK fusion cancer treatment in the age of TRK-targeted therapy.

items.title: Bone metastases identify a high-risk subgroup in metastatic neuroendocrine tumors with particular relevance in NETs of unknown primary.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bone metastases (BM) are an increasingly recognized manifestation of advanced neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), but their prevalence and association with survival in NETs of unknown primary (CUP NET) remain insufficiently characterized. We assessed the prevalence of BM and their association with overall survival (OS) in patients with metastatic pancreatic NETs (PanNETs), small intestinal NETs (siNETs), and CUP NETs.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 642 patients with histologically confirmed metastatic well-differentiated NETs who were treated at the European Neuroendocrine Tumour Society (ENETS) Center Essen between 2009 and 2023 using somatostatin-receptor (SSTR)- based hybrid imaging with 68Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT. The patients included 171 with PanNETs, 305 with siNETs, and 166 with CUP NETs. The primary outcome was OS, defined as the time from date of initial NET diagnosis to death from any cause. Secondary outcomes included BM prevalence, entity-specific survival according to BM status, BM morphology and timing, and skeletal-related events.
RESULTS: BM were detected in 238 patients (37.1%) and were most frequent in CUP NETs (42.8%), followed by PanNETs (36.3%) and siNETs (34.4%). Median OS in the overall cohort was 77 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 64-89) in patients with BM and 141 months (95% CI, 119-186) in metastatic patients without BM (log-rank p < 0.001). In CUP NETs, median OS was 30 months in patients with BM and 66 months in metastatic patients without BM (log-rank p = 0.021). In multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, tumor grade, functioning status, and tumor entity, BM remained associated with shorter OS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.45; 95% CI, 1.13-1.85; p = 0.0034). In an entity-stratified model BM remained associated with OS (HR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.09-1.89; p = 0.011). In the CUP NET subgroup, the adjusted HR associated with BM was 1.83 (95% CI, 1.17-2.85; p = 0.008).
CONCLUSION: BM were common in patients with metastatic NETs and are particularly prevalent and clinically relevant in CUP NET.

items.title: Mechanosensitive epitranscriptomics in cancer: linking tumor mechanics, RNA modification, and immune escape.
items.abstract: Solid tumors are mechanically abnormal ecosystems in which extracellular matrix stiffening, compressive stress, interstitial pressure, and aberrant fluid flow reshape cancer, stromal, and immune cell behavior. In parallel, the cancer epitranscriptome has emerged as a dynamic regulatory layer in which RNA modifications, including m6A, m5C, m7G, pseudouridine, and A-to-I editing, control RNA stability, translation, splicing, localization, and immune recognition. This review proposes mechanosensitive epitranscriptomics as an integrative framework linking these two fields. We discuss how canonical mechanotransduction pathways, including integrin-FAK signaling, YAP/TAZ activation, PIEZO1-mediated calcium influx, cytoskeletal remodeling, and nuclear deformation, may converge on RNA writers, erasers, readers, editing enzymes, RNA-binding proteins, noncoding RNAs, and ribonucleoprotein condensates. Particular emphasis is placed on the tumor-immune interface, where mechanical stress and RNA modifications jointly influence antigen presentation, interferon signaling, checkpoint expression, metabolic adaptation, T-cell and NK-cell function, myeloid polarization, and immune exclusion. At present, two representative studies in the evidence set reviewed here meet the Tier-1 definition in cancer-relevant systems: the PDAC stiffness-METTL14/IGF2BP3-YAP1 study and the macrophage stiffness-FTO-Socs1 study, whereas most broader cancer-specific links remain Tier-3 hypotheses or mechanically confounded associations. We highlight evidence gaps and propose testable models to distinguish direct mechanoregulation from secondary effects of hypoxia, inflammation, and metabolism. Finally, we outline experimental and translational strategies for mapping mechanical niches, defining causal RNA-modification circuits, and developing composite biomarkers that integrate tumor mechanics, epitranscriptomic states, and immunotherapy response.

items.title: From arterial resection to the TRIANGLE operation: a bibliometric analysis of radical periarterial surgery for pancreatic cancer
items.abstract: Purpose Radical periarterial techniques, including artery-first approaches, mesopancreas excision, arterial resection, periarterial divestment and the TRIANGLE operation, address the same periarterial compartment under different names, and their literature has not been mapped as a whole. This study aimed to map the growth, contributors, collaboration patterns, thematic evolution and randomized evidence of this field. Methods The Web of Science Core Collection was searched on 6 October 2026 for English-language articles and reviews. After title and abstract screening, 539 records were analysed. Performance indicators were calculated, and co-authorship and keyword co-occurrence networks were built with VOSviewer. Reporting followed the BIBLIO guideline. Results The 539 documents (2000–2026) appeared in 128 journals and received 13,491 citations (h-index 56). Annual output grew by 14.4% per year between 2010 and 2025. Japan contributed the most documents (n = 161) but had the lowest international collaboration rate among the leading countries (2.1%). Heidelberg University was the most productive and most cited institution. The co-authorship network comprised 11 clusters, led by Japanese groups and a Heidelberg-centred European group. Arterial divestment, conversion surgery, robotic surgery and the TRIANGLE operation were among the newest themes. Only three completed randomized controlled trials were identified, all testing artery-first approaches; none addressed the TRIANGLE operation, divestment or arterial resection. Conclusion Research on radical periarterial pancreatic surgery has moved from extended en bloc resection to neoadjuvant-enabled, artery-preserving clearance, yet these operations rest almost entirely on non-randomized evidence. Standardized definitions of periarterial clearance and multinational randomized trials are needed.

items.title: Cancer Risks Associated With Germline BARD1 Pathogenic/Likely Pathogenic Variants: A Multicenter Study of 445 Families.
items.abstract:
PURPOSE: To estimate the relative and absolute risks (ARs) for ovarian, prostate, male and female breast, pancreatic, biliary tract, and colorectal cancers associated with germline BARD1 pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants (PVs/LPVs) because these risks have not previously been reported from a genotype-first perspective.
METHODS: We performed a secondary retrospective analysis of multicenter data comprising 445 three-generation pedigrees with confirmed BARD1 PVs/LPVs from 25 institutions nationwide. Data were aggregated at the family-relatedness level. The risks were estimated using a Bayesian survival model that incorporated information from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program.
RESULTS: We confirmed the previously established increased risk for female breast cancer (relative risk [RR] = 3.53; 95% CI, 1.95 to 5.81; posterior probability [PP] = 0.0040) and found positive associations with female pancreatic cancer (RR = 3.76 [95% CI, 2.16-7.25]; PP < .0001), male pancreatic cancer (RR = 2.89 [95% CI, 1.66 to 5.61]; PP < .0001), and prostate cancer (RR = 3.02 [95% CI, 1.95 to 4.71]; PP < .0001). The predictive ARs to age 85 were 41.84% (95% CI, 23.09 to 68.91) for female breast cancer, 4.80% (95% CI, 2.76 to 9.25) for female pancreatic cancer, 3.98% (95% CI, 2.29 to 7.73) for male pancreatic cancer, and 36.11% (95% CI, 23.29 to 56.29) for prostate cancer. Risk estimates suggest an association for male breast, ovarian, and female colorectal cancers; however, the clinical significance is unclear, and these findings warrant cautious interpretation. In contrast, we found no evidence of association for biliary tract cancer or male colorectal cancer.
CONCLUSION: These results support BARD1's association with female breast cancer and suggest associations with pancreatic and prostate cancers. These findings have potential implications for genetic counseling and personalized risk management for male and female BARD1 PV/LPV heterozygotes.

items.title: Gemcitabine Delivery and Nucleolin-Targeting Nanocarriers Based on N6L-Functionalized Polyelectrolyte Complexes and Layer-By-Layer Lipid Nanoparticles.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is highly resistant to chemotherapy due to dense stromal barriers. Although gemcitabine remains the standard treatment, its efficacy is limited. Combining it with the pseudopeptide N6L has shown synergistic effects, but administering them individually in biological systems poses significant challenges. To overcome this, we developed a polyanion-gemcitabine conjugate (PAAGem) coupled with N6L, a multivalent cationic ligand with intrinsic anticancer activity. The conjugation was confirmed, and gemcitabine retained its biological activity post-grafting. Quartz crystal microbalance studies revealed electrostatic interactions between PAAGem and N6L, guiding nanoparticle assembly. Building on this strategy, we engineered two electrostatic nanosystems: (i) a multilayer architecture constructed on nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) via a layer-by-layer approach, enabling controlled incorporation of cytotoxic agents, and (ii) a simpler polyelectrolyte complex (PEC) formed by spontaneous co-assembly in aqueous media. Colloidal analyses showed superior stability of LbL-NLCs. In murine PDAC cells, LbL-NLCs exhibited markedly enhanced anticancer efficacy compared with free gemcitabine + N6L, whereas PEC formulations provided limited improvement. These results were further validated in vivo. Overall, our study demonstrates that electrostatic multilayer architectures leveraging PAAGem-N6L interactions significantly outperform simple electrostatic complexes, highlighting LbL-functionalized NLCs as a promising nanotherapeutic strategy for PDAC treatment.

items.title: Adipocyte-derived FABP4 Drives Pancreatic Cancer Radioresistance via FABP4- eIF3a Axis
items.abstract: Background Radiotherapy is a common treatment modality for patients with locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer, but the therapeutic efficacy is constrained by intrinsic radioresistance. The tumor microenvironment, particularly peritumoral adipose tissue, plays a critical yet poorly understood role in modulating therapeutic responses. Methods Peritumoral adipose tissue distribution in pancreatic cancer was assessed by H&E staining. The effects of adipocytes on cancer cell radiosensitivity were evaluated using a co-culture system combined with colony formation, alkaline comet, and flow cytometry assays. Energy metabolism, lipid accumulation, and fatty acid transporter levels in co-cultured cancer cells were examined by Seahorse analysis, BODIPY staining, real-time PCR, and immunofluorescence. The role of FABP4 in adipocyte-mediated radiosensitivity regulation was tested using FABP4-knockout 3T3-L1 cells, exogenous FABP4 protein, and a FABP4 inhibitor. FABP4-overexpressing cancer cells and nude mouse xenografts were used to determine the effects of FABP4 on radiosensitivity. Underlying mechanisms were explored and validated by Co-IP, LC-MS/MS, RIP, and other approaches. Results The results of the pathology showed that the pancreatic cancer was surrounded by peripancreatic adipose tissue. Co-culture with adipocytes significantly enhancing clonogenic survival of pancreatic cancer cells while attenuated radiation-induced DNA damage, apoptosis, and G2/M arrest, an effect mediated by FABP4. Genetic ablation of FABP4 in adipocytes abolished this radioprotection, whereas exogenous FABP4 supplementation or its overexpression recapitulated radioresistance both in vitro and in vivo. Proteomic screening identified eIF3a as the predominant FABP4-interacting protein. Functional validation demonstrated that eIF3a knockdown abrogated the FABP4-enhanced radioresistance, confirming its essential role in this process. EIF3a knockdown increased KU80 and MRE11 expression and promoted radioresistance, whereas FABP4 suppressed KU80 and MRE11 expression by enhancing eIF3a–mRNA binding. Conclusions This study identify adipocyte‑derived FABP4 as a pivotal regulator of pancreatic cancer radiosensitivity and unveil the FABP4–eIF3a axis as a potential therapeutic target for radiosensitization.

items.title: SVP Maps Spatially Variable Functional Programs and Their Coupling in Spatial Transcriptomics.
items.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics has made tissue architecture measurable at molecular resolution, yet most computational methods still identify spatially variable genes and infer biology only indirectly. We present SVP, a framework that directly maps spatially variable cell states, pathways and regulatory programs from spatial transcriptomic data. SVP combines location-level functional activity inference with global and local spatial autocorrelation and extends these analyses to bivariate spatial coupling across heterogeneous features. Across simulations and real datasets, SVP recovered cell-state-associated activity patterns at individual captured locations, detected spatially variable features with calibrated statistics, and scaled efficiently to large datasets. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, SVP identified a spatially co-organized hypoxic and extracellular-matrix-remodeling niche that co-localized with regions of low immune activity. It further captured functional maturation in the developing human heart and plaque-associated glial programs in Alzheimer's disease models. SVP enables direct analysis of functional spatial organization, moving beyond gene-centric descriptions of tissue structure.

Causal Links Between Seborrheic Keratosis and Internal Malignancies: Evidence from Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The association between seborrheic keratosis (SK) and internal malignancies remains controversial, with findings from observational studies often confounded by reverse causality and unmeasured confounding factors. This study aimed to investigate the causal relationship between SK and common malignancies using a bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) approach.
METHODS: Genetic instruments for SK and malignancies (thyroid, breast, lung, colorectal, liver, gastric, prostate, renal, and pancreatic cancer) were derived from publicly available genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics based on individuals of European ancestry. Independent single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) significantly associated with SK were used as instrumental variables. Bidirectional two-sample MR analyses were performed, primarily using the inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method, supplemented by MR-Egger, weighted median, and other robust methods. Sensitivity analyses, including Cochran's Q test, MR-Egger intercept test, and leave-one-out analysis, were conducted to assess heterogeneity, pleiotropy, and the robustness of the results.
RESULTS: In the present study, genetically predicted SK was associated with an increased risk of breast cancer (IVW OR = 1.075, 95% CI: 1.014-1.139, P = 0.015) and colorectal cancer (IVW OR = 1.211, 95% CI: 1.069-1.371, P = 0.003). No significant causal associations were found between SK and the other seven cancers. Sensitivity analyses revealed no significant horizontal pleiotropy, and the results were robust. Reverse MR analysis did not support a causal effect of the investigated cancers on SK.
CONCLUSION: This study provides genetic evidence supporting a potential causal association between SK and increased risk of breast and colorectal cancer. These findings offer new insights into the clinical significance of SK, although the underlying biological mechanisms require further elucidation.

items.title: Quicklime Slaking-Mediated Exothermic Reactions in Polidocanol-Integrated Ablators with Inhibited Heat Diffusion Enable Cancer Thermal Ablation.
items.abstract: Despite showing a wide application in tumor therapy, the clinically-used exogenous thermal ablation still suffers from uncontrollable temperature field with rapid heat diffusion. Here an endogenous trigger-encouraged thermal ablation, namely exothermic reaction-based thermal ablation (ERTA) based on quicklime slaking and acid-base neutralization reactions, has been established, wherein CaO nanoparticles were encapsulated with Ag nanoparticles by liposomes to construct ERTA ablators. CaO consumes H2O and H+ after exothermic reactions to give birth to Ca2+ and heat. Liposome shell prolongs ERTA via limiting the exothermic reaction rate, and intracellular Ca2+ overload unites with Ag nanoparticles to produce antitumor ROS to boost cancer ERTA. Importantly, polidocanol-based foam sclerosing agent (PFSA) with low heat conductivity was integrated to inhibit heat diffusion and confine heat in tumor to elevate temperature and enhance ERTA efficiency. Additionally, PFSA as a routine clinical embolism agent destroys intratumoral blood vessels to occlude blood vessels and establish starvation therapy, which further improves PFSA-enhanced ERTA efficiency. Consequently, such ERTA-based ablators and PFSA-integrated ones outperform the scale-matched microwave ablation and laboratory-in photothermal ablation in repressing subcutaneous and orthotopic hepatocellular carcinoma, and orthotopic pancreatic cancer. This endogenous trigger-activated thermal ablation method provides distinctive insights into thermal ablation, presenting a new thermal ablation protocol.

items.title: Physics-Constrained Conformal Screening: A Certified Machine Learning Framework for the Rational Design of Dual Glycoepitope-Imprinted Polymers Recognizing CA 19-9 and MUC1-Tn.
items.abstract: The selectivity of a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) is decided the moment its functional monomer is chosen, yet that choice is still made largely by trial and error and without any statement of confidence, so a confident but wrong pick can commit months of synthesis before it fails. We recast the role of artificial intelligence in this problem: rather than predicting a binding value, which the scarce, noisy data of pre-synthetic screening cannot support, the learning layer issues a distribution-free certificate on the decision itself. We realize this as physics-constrained conformal screening, a fully in silico framework that returns not a ranked guess but a certified shortlist provably holding the best monomer. Site-directed monomer and template complexes are relaxed with the GFN2-xTB tight-binding Hamiltonian in implicit water; a competition-corrected score, Scomp, discounts monomer self-association and solvation; a best-of-k estimator measures how far the sampling has converged; and a distribution-free conformal bound turns the result into a candidate set guaranteed, with controlled probability, to contain the optimal monomer. We prove that the corrected estimator is one-sided exact, so only the lower bound needs calibration and the guarantee requires no correction for the size of the library, and we show that a single calibration transfers between targets. Applied to two pancreatic cancer glycoepitopes, sialyl-Lewisa, the carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA 19-9) determinant, and the mucin 1 (MUC1) Tn antigen (MUC1-Tn), the framework contracts a twenty-monomer library to two and five certified candidates at ninety-percent confidence while cutting compute by 35 to 67 percent, and it identifies 3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene (EDOT) and 3-aminophenylboronic acid (3-APBA) as certified affinity optima. The same multi-seed certificate then separates the selectivity claims it can support, EDOT reading the sialylation of sialyl-Lewisa and 4-aminophenylboronic acid (4-APBA) reading the Tn-glycosylation of MUC1, from the harder sialyl-Lewisx regioisomer discrimination, which it flags as under-determined rather than passing off an under-sampled gap as a decisive hit, a distinction an uncertified screen cannot make. Strikingly, no point prediction model beats a trivial baseline while certification succeeds, which locates the dependable value of machine learning, for cheap physics in a low-data regime, in a guarantee rather than a guess.

items.title: Nanoparticles Using Lavender and Rosemary Extracts as Reducing Agent: Physicochemical Characterization and Antiproliferative Activity Against Human Cancer Cells.
items.abstract: Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) synthesized using plant extracts represent a promising approach combining environmentally friendly nanoparticle synthesis with potential biomedical applications. In this study, AgNPs were synthesized using aqueous extracts of dried Lavandula angustifolia (LEx) and Salvia rosmarinus (REx) leaves, physicochemically characterized, and evaluated for their antiproliferative activity against six human cancer cell lines and one non-tumorigenic human cell line. HPLC analysis revealed distinct phytochemical profiles of the two extracts, while UV-Vis, FTIR, TEM, SAED, and SEM-EDX analyses were used to characterize the resulting lavender-mediated (LAg) and rosemary-mediated (RAg) AgNPs. TEM analysis showed a greater proportion of smaller nanoparticles in RAg than in LAg. Antiproliferative activity was evaluated using the MTT assay after 48 h of exposure, with LEx, REx, and AgNO3 included as controls. Both AgNP formulations exhibited cell-line-dependent activity. LAg reached IC50 values of 19.4-20.8 µmol Ag/L in five cancer cell lines, whereas RAg reached IC50 values of 14.4-25.2 µmol Ag/L. The lowest IC50 was observed for RAg in PaTu 8902 pancreatic adenocarcinoma cells (14.4 ± 0.6 µmol Ag/L). In contrast, the IC50 was not reached in A549 or non-tumorigenic CCD-18Co cells at concentrations up to 50 µmol Ag/L (IC50 > 50 µmol Ag/L). Neither LEx nor REx produced 50% inhibition of cell viability at concentrations up to 1.7% (v/v). Similarly, AgNO3 did not achieve 50% inhibition at concentrations up to 50 µmol/L in any of the cell lines tested. These findings demonstrate formulation- and cell-line-dependent antiproliferative activity of green-synthesized AgNPs and support further investigation of their biological effects and underlying mechanisms.

items.title: Polarity-Guided Extraction of Crithmum maritimum L.: Phenolic Profiling, Selective Anticancer Activity in AR42J and HT-29 Cells, and Antimicrobial Effects.
items.abstract: Crithmum maritimum L. (sea fennel) (C. maritimum) is a halophyte plant rich in phenolic compounds, flavonoids, essential oils, and other secondary metabolites. Despite its traditional medicinal use, no study has comprehensively compared multiple solvent extracts of C. maritimum across diverse cancer and non-cancerous cell lines, leaving its solvent-dependent cytotoxic potential and selectivity largely uncharacterized. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the biochemical composition of different extracts of C. maritimum (obtained using ethanol, ethyl acetate, and distilled water) and the cytotoxic effects of these extracts on pancreatic cancer (AR42J) and colon cancer (HT-29) cell lines, compared to a healthy cell line (ARPE19). Additionally, we determined the extracts' antimicrobial activity against various bacteria and a fungal species. Ethanol yielded the richest and most diverse phenolic profile in C. maritimum, while ethyl acetate extracted moderate levels, and the aqueous extract contained only minor amounts, demonstrating that solvent polarity strongly influences the recovery of bioactive phenolic compounds. Ethanol extracts showed the strongest and most consistent cytotoxicity across normal and cancer cells, while ethyl acetate extracts exhibited high and selective activity on cancer cells. Water extract demonstrated selective cytotoxic effects during prolonged incubations. The extracts displayed solvent-dependent antimicrobial activity, with ethanol and ethyl acetate fractions showing potent inhibition, particularly against Yersinia pseudotuberculosis, Candida albicans, and Staphylococcus aureus. In contrast, the water extract showed no activity. Overall, the findings indicate that C. maritimum contains bioactive constituents with selective cytotoxicity against cancer cells and microorganisms, depending on the extraction solvent, supporting its potential as a source of natural anticancer and antimicrobial agents.

items.title: Evaluation of the Cytotoxic and Apoptotic Activities and the Phytochemical Profile of Euphorbia indivisa (Engelm) Tidestr.
items.abstract: Cancer remains one of the leading causes of death worldwide, highlighting the need to develop new therapeutic strategies. In this context, several species of the Euphorbiaceae family have demonstrated cytotoxic activity. The present study evaluated the cytotoxic effect of Euphorbia indivisa on three cancer cell lines (Breast cancer, MCF-7; Human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, PANC-1; Human cervical, SiHa), as well as on a nontumorigenic cell line (Immortalized human keratinocyte, HaCaT). The chemical profile of the species was also determined. The hydroalcoholic extract (HAE) and fractions were obtained by maceration and liquid-liquid partitioning using dichloromethane (DCF), ethyl acetate (EAF), and butanol (BuF). Cell confluence and death were determined by analysis of images from cells stained with Propidium iodide (PI). The apoptotic effect was evaluated by Annexin V/7-Amine-Actinomycin D (AAD) staining and caspase-3/7. Antiproliferative activity was determined by Carboxyfluorescein succinimidyl ester (CFSE) staining. The extract, fractions, and aqueous residue (AR) exhibited cytotoxic activity against the PANC-1 cell line, with EAF showing the highest activity, demonstrating an IC50 of 26.27 µg/mL. In contrast, EAF showed lower cytotoxicity against HaCaT cells. Likewise, EAF inhibited proliferation and induced cell death via apoptosis in a concentration-dependent manner. β-sitosterol, palmitic acid, and apigenin-8-C-glucoside were isolated from EAF, whereas quercetin and gallic acid were identified in a mixture obtained from this fraction. Therefore, this species could be considered as an important source for cancer therapy.

items.title: Trends and Patterns in Gastrointestinal Cancer Burden in Asia, 1990-2023: Evidence from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal cancers are among the leading causes of cancer incidence and mortality worldwide and represent a major contributor to the cancer burden in Asia. This study aims to assess the burden of six major gastrointestinal cancers in Asia from 1990 to 2023.
METHODS: Based on the Global Burden of Disease 2023 data, we analyzed the incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of six major gastrointestinal cancers-esophageal cancer (EC), stomach cancer (SC), colon and rectum cancer (CRC), liver cancer (LC), pancreatic cancer (PC), and gallbladder and biliary tract cancer (GBTC)-from 1990 to 2023.
RESULTS: In 2023, Asia reported about 3.23 million new gastrointestinal cancer cases and 2.26 million deaths, resulting in 55.10 million DALYs. EC had the highest burden in East Asia [age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR): 11.41 per 100,000; age-standardized death rate (ASDR): 10.88 per 100,000; age-standardized DALY rate (ASDALYR): 244.41 per 100,000], while CRC, PC, and GBTC had a high burden in the high-income Asia-Pacific region. From 1990 to 2023, EC, LC, and GBTC declined in most regions, whereas PC increased except in East Asia. The burden was generally higher in males; however, in South Asia, females had higher ASIR (3.35 per 100,000), ASDR (3.44 per 100,000), and ASDALYR (82.94 per 100,000) for GBTC than males.
CONCLUSIONS: The burden of gastrointestinal cancer in Asia is heavy and unevenly distributed; in the future, more targeted regional prevention and control strategies should be implemented based on socioeconomic levels and the characteristics of the disease spectrum.

items.title: Identification of Candidate Partner Cells in Tumor-Stromal Interactions by Histology-Based Spatial Analysis for Prognostic Stratification After Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy.
items.abstract: Despite advances in multidisciplinary treatment, recurrence remains a major clinical challenge in refractory cancers. Many patients have residual tumor after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC), and clinical outcomes among patients without a pathological complete response (non-pCR) are heterogeneous. The spatial relationships between residual tumor cells and surrounding stromal cells may provide information for further prognostic stratification. In this review, we discuss histology-based spatial analysis (HSA) of surgical specimens, with particular attention to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. We describe four steps that connect existing biological, histological, and clinical findings. First, intercellular distances and local cell numbers are compared to identify candidate partner cells. Second, functional and molecular studies examine their interactions with tumor cells, including effects on survival and drug resistance. Third, HSA of immunostained patient specimens measures the number, size, and localization of foci containing cell relationships supported by these studies. Fourth, these measurements are evaluated in relation to recurrence and survival, alongside established clinicopathological factors. This approach uses archival surgical specimens to connect biological findings with patient outcomes. Its value for prognostic stratification after NAC requires validation in large clinical cohorts.

items.title: Aldo-keto reductase family 1 member B10 in solid tumors: lipid metabolic reprogramming, immune remodeling, and targeted therapy.
items.abstract: Aldo-keto reductase family 1 member B10 (AKR1B10), an NADPH-dependent aldo-keto reductase, has emerged as a context-dependent metabolic stress regulator with important implications for therapeutic resistance and tumor immune remodeling in solid tumors. By neutralizing lipid-derived aldehydes such as 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE), AKR1B10 limits lipid-derived carbonyl stress and may reduce ferroptosis susceptibility in defined tumor contexts. It also stabilizes acetyl-CoA carboxylase α, thereby sustaining de novo lipogenesis (DNL). In addition, AKR1B10 has been linked to increased glycolysis-associated lactate production in specific tumor settings. This increase in lactate can promote histone lactylation-mediated epigenetic reprogramming. Together with reported associations between AKR1B10 and immune-cell infiltration or function, these metabolic effects may contribute to tumor immune remodeling in a context-dependent manner. Aberrant AKR1B10 expression has been associated with tumor progression and therapeutic resistance in several solid tumors, including hepatocellular carcinoma, non-small-cell lung cancer, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, and cholangiocarcinoma. This review systematically examines the structural biology, transcriptional regulation, and tumor-intrinsic and microenvironmental functions of AKR1B10. It further evaluates its tumor-type-specific diagnostic and prognostic potential and discusses emerging inhibitor strategies. Nonetheless, key challenges remain, including the tissue-specific functional duality of AKR1B10, the demand for inhibitors selective over the structurally homologous AKR1B1, and limited causal evidence linking AKR1B10 to immune remodeling in tumors. Future research should integrate multimodal spatial omics, immunocompetent tumor models, and rational combination therapy designs to advance AKR1B10 from a metabolic enzyme into a clinically actionable target for precision oncology.

items.title: Pathologic and Molecular Characterization of Branch Duct Intraductal Papillary Mucinous Neoplasm With Advanced Neoplasia Under-Recognized by Kyoto High-Risk Stigmata.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Kyoto high-risk stigmata (HRS) guide resection of branch-duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (BD-IPMNs) but miss a substantial proportion of high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma (HGD/IC). We characterized the pathologic, molecular, and anatomic features of HGD/IC that Kyoto HRS fail to identify, and examined whether they are detectable before surgery by endoscopic ultrasound-guided needle-based confocal laser endomicroscopy (EUS-nCLE) and cyst-fluid molecular analysis.
METHODS: BD-IPMNs resected from 2015 to 2024 in two prospective trials were retrospectively analyzed. Dysplasia and IPMN-subtype were reassessed by blinded pancreaticobiliary pathologists with consensus and immunohistochemistry. Papillary architecture was classified as macropapillary versus non-macropapillary (micropapillary or flat). Diagnostic performance for HGD/IC was assessed against the consensus pathology reference standard.
RESULTS: Among 68 BD-IPMNs, 26 (38.2%) had HGD/IC, concentrated in non-macropapillary lesions (53.1%, 17/32, vs. 25.0%, 9/36; P=0.017), with the micropapillary pattern carrying the highest proportion (71.4%, 10/14). GNAS mutation was less frequent in non-macropapillary than macropapillary lesions (25.0% vs. 85.2%; P<0.001). Kyoto HRS were highly specific (95.2%) but only 53.8% sensitive; among 52 HRS-negative lesions, 23.1% (12/52) harbored HGD/IC, predominantly non-macropapillary, GNAS-negative, and located in the body or tail. Adding EUS-nCLE raised sensitivity from 52% to 80% (McNemar P=0.016) at 81% specificity, but nCLE was least sensitive in non-macropapillary lesions (43.8%), where absent GNAS provided a complementary preoperative marker.
CONCLUSIONS: The HGD/IC missed by Kyoto HRS was characteristically micropapillary, GNAS-negative, and/or in the body or tail. Because architecture and subtype are histopathologic, preoperative recognition rests on combining Kyoto HRS, EUS-nCLE, and cyst-fluid molecular testing. Prospective external validation is warranted.

items.title: 7MeERT Engages PSMD14-Associated Proteasome Lid Components and Suppresses Glycolysis via K63-Linked Ubiquitination and PKM2 Nuclear Exclusion.
items.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Altered energy metabolism is a central feature of cancer. Among ubiquitin-dependent regulatory mechanisms, K63-linked ubiquitination has attracted attention as a non-proteolytic means of modulating metabolic enzymes. PSMD14 (Rpn11), a JAMM-family deubiquitinase located in the 19S proteasome lid, has been linked to malignant progression, but the role of pharmacological perturbation of PSMD14-associated proteasome lid biology in cancer metabolism has not been fully defined.
METHODS: To examine the metabolic effects of 7MeERT, an Ertredin derivative, we performed extracellular flux assays in multiple cancer cell types. Drug-protein engagement was assessed using lysate-based DARTS and CETSA. Changes in ubiquitination and PKM2 localization were analyzed by immunoblotting, TUBE2 pulldown, and confocal immunofluorescence analysis, and PSMD14 knockdown was used to examine the mechanism.
RESULTS: 7MeERT reduced basal and/or compensatory glycolysis in glioblastoma, triple-negative breast cancer, and pancreatic cancer cells. Lysate-based DARTS and CETSA supported engagement of PSMD14 and other proteasome lid subunits by 7MeERT, whereas the base subunit PSMC2 was unaffected. In contrast to MG132, 7MeERT did not cause broad accumulation of ubiquitinated proteins. Instead, it preferentially increased K63-linked ubiquitination, enhanced PKM2 ubiquitination, and decreased nuclear PKM2 localization. PSMD14 knockdown reproduced the K63-linked ubiquitination, PKM2 localization, and glycolytic phenotypes associated with 7MeERT treatment. In addition, 7MeERT more strongly suppressed the proliferation of TNBC cells with relatively high PSMD14 expression than that of normal mammary epithelial cells.
DISCUSSION: These data support a model in which engagement of PSMD14-associated proteasome lid components perturbs non-proteolytic ubiquitin signaling and disrupts PKM2-linked glycolytic regulation in cancer cells.
CONCLUSION: 7MeERT suppresses cancer cell glycolysis in association with engagement of PSMD14- associated proteasome lid components and alterations in K63-linked ubiquitination and PKM2 nuclear localization. This mechanism suggests that modulation of PSMD14-associated deubiquitination may provide an approach distinct from conventional proteasome inhibition.

items.title: Palliative care utilization among adults hospitalized with metastatic gastrointestinal malignancies in the United States, 2016 to 2022: national trends, cancer-type variation, and predictors of consultation.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Palliative care (PC) is integral to goal-concordant care for patients with advanced cancer, yet inpatient consultation remains inconsistently utilized. Contemporary national data on cancer-specific differences and factors associated with PC utilization in metastatic gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies are limited.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of adult hospitalizations (2016-2022) from the National Inpatient Sample, identifying metastatic GI cancers using ICD-10 codes and PC consultation by code Z51.5. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) controlling for demographics, cancer type, comorbidity, and hospital characteristics. Prespecified models were fitted for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and colorectal cancer (CRC). Secular trends were quantified using joinpoint regression.
RESULTS: Overall, 20.6% of hospitalizations involved PC consultation, rising from 19.2% (2016) to 23.9% (2022; annual percentage change 3.47%, P < 0.001). Rates ranged from 17.0% (CRC) to 32.1% (HCC). Compared with CRC, odds of PC were significantly higher for HCC (aOR 3.98), cholangiocarcinoma (aOR 2.63), pancreatic cancer (aOR 2.61), esophageal cancer (aOR 2.33), and gallbladder cancer (aOR 1.78; all P < 0.001). Black adults had higher odds than White adults (aOR 1.17). Medicare (aOR 0.70) and private insurance (aOR 0.80) had lower odds compared with Medicaid. Urban hospitals had higher utilization than rural hospitals. Higher comorbidity burden demonstrated a stepwise association with increased PC use. Cancer-specific models revealed distinct demographic and institutional predictors for CRC and HCC.
CONCLUSIONS: Inpatient PC for metastatic GI cancers remains underutilized, with wide variation by cancer type, insurance, region, and hospital characteristics, underscoring the need for structured, diagnosis-specific consultation pathways.

Mortality in sepsis among patients with gastrointestinal malignancies: a nationwide analysis 2017-2021.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies, with in-hospital mortality rates of 19.8% to 28%, significantly higher than in non-cancer patients. While sepsis outcomes have been extensively studied in the general population, large-scale population-level analyses specific to GI cancers remain limited. This study aimed to identify the outcomes of sepsis in gastric, colon, hepatic, and pancreatic cancers in the United States.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of the National Inpatient Sample (2017-2021) using ICD-10 codes, including adults ≥18 years with gastric (n=205,599), colon (n=851,120), hepatocellular (n=433,145), or pancreatic (n=557,204) cancer. Propensity matching and multivariate regression were used to adjust for confounders. A p-value of ≤0.05 was considered significant.
RESULTS: Sepsis prevalence was 13.79% in gastric, 12.6% in colon, 18.76% in hepatocellular, and 19.22% in pancreatic cancer hospitalizations. In-hospital mortality was significantly higher with sepsis across all four malignancies (gastric 23.57% vs. 5.09%; colon 17.72% vs. 2.74%; hepatocellular 22.34% vs. 6.22%; pancreatic 17.26% vs. 5.11%). After propensity matching and adjustment, sepsis was independently associated with increased mortality in gastric (aOR 1.87), colon (aOR 2.39), hepatocellular (aOR 1.60), and pancreatic cancer (aOR 1.43) (all p<0.001). Mortality among patients requiring ICU-level care was 70.28%, 70.88%, 72.97%, and 67%, respectively. Acute kidney injury, acute respiratory failure, invasive ventilation, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and shock were consistent mortality predictors across all malignancies (p<0.05). Sepsis was also associated with significantly higher hospitalization charges and longer length of stay (p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Our study revealed that patients with gastrointestinal malignancies experience high mortality rates when affected by sepsis, with acute organ dysfunction and ICU-level care as key predictors of poor outcomes. These findings highlight GI cancer as a high-risk population for adverse sepsis outcomes and support the need for prospective studies evaluating early recognition and guideline-directed therapies.

items.title: A New Optimal Cut-Points Selection Method for Diseases With Multiple Ordinal Stages and Its Confidence Interval Estimation.
items.abstract: Optimal cut-points selection plays a fundamental role in multi-stage classification. The popular Youden index method primarily emphasizes overall diagnostic accuracy while overlooking imbalance among classification rates across disease stages, whereas other methods improve balance at the cost of substantially reduced overall accuracy. Such trade-offs are undesirable in clinical decision-making. This article aims to develop a flexible optimal cut-points selection method that simultaneously preserves overall diagnostic accuracy and balance among stage-specific classification rates. By introducing a tuning parameter, the proposed method integrates the arithmetic mean and the geometric mean of stage-specific classification rates into a unified objective function. Estimation procedures for confidence intervals are developed under both parametric and nonparametric settings. Simulation studies are conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed cut-points selection method and the confidence interval estimation approaches. The proposed method is applied to a real pancreatic cancer dataset to illustrate its practical utility.

items.title: Endoscopic Drainage of An Intra-Abdominal Chylous Collection.
items.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chylous leak is an increasingly recognised complication following pancreatic surgery. It results from the disruption of the lymphatic system and may lead to persistent chylous ascites or collection. Ongoing chyle loss is associated with significant morbidity including malnutrition, dehydration, electrolyte disturbance, hypoalbuminaemia, immunosuppression and impaired wound healing. Clinicians managing patients in the perioperative setting should remain vigilant for the development of chylous leak, particularly following high-risk surgery. While most cases respond to conservative management with dietary modification and use of somatostatin analogues, refractory cases remain challenging and may require technically demanding or morbid interventions. We report a novel minimally invasive approach using endoscopic ultrasound-guided cyst gastrostomy for a post-operative chylous collection.
CASE DESCRIPTION: A 53-year-old woman underwent distal pancreatectomy, splenectomy and lymph node clearance for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with associated extensive lymphadenopathy. On post-operative day seven, she developed abdominal pain and elevated inflammatory markers. Computed tomography demonstrated a 14 × 5 cm thin-walled collection within the lesser sac. Percutaneous drainage yielded turbid milky fluid consistent with chyle. Despite initial conservative management, a persistent high output chyle leak developed. EUS-guided cyst gastrostomy was performed, allowing internal drainage of chyle into the stomach. The patient recovered without complications, resumed oral intake and was discharged two days following the procedure.
CONCLUSION: EUS-guided cyst gastrostomy may represent a safe, minimally invasive therapeutic option for selected patients with persistent chylous collections. This approach may mitigate risks associated with prolonged or repeated external drainage and facilitate earlier discharge, allowing ongoing outpatient conservative management.
LEARNING POINTS: Post-operative chylous leak and chylous collections are associated with significant morbidity, particularly when diagnosis is delayed. Perioperative medical teams should maintain a high index of suspicion and actively monitor for this complication following high-risk surgery.Persistent chyle loss can lead to malnutrition, dehydration, electrolyte disturbances, immunosuppression, hypoalbuminaemia and impaired wound healing, highlighting the importance of early nutritional, fluid and electrolyte support.Endoscopic ultrasound-guided cyst gastrostomy may represent a safe, minimally invasive alternative which allows internal drainage of a chylous collection, ameliorating risks associated with repeated or prolonged external drainage.

items.title: PLA2G2A across tumor compartments and its relevance to drug resistance.
items.abstract: Drug resistance in cancer is shaped not only by tumor-cell-intrinsic mutations but also by spatially organized microenvironmental states. PLA2G2A, encoding group IIA secreted phospholipase A2 (sPLA2-IIA), is usually discussed as an inflammatory lipid enzyme; however, its cancer relevance depends strongly on cellular source, localization and disease stage. This Review uses a compartment-resolved framework that annotates four domains - source, spatial niche, linked biochemical output and functional or therapy-response phenotype - and separates PLA2G2A-specific mechanistic evidence from evidence for therapy or immune resistance. Several cancer studies provide PLA2G2A-specific functional evidence for invasion, proliferation/stemness, non-catalytic signaling or T-cell dysfunction, but direct demonstration that PLA2G2A changes response to a defined anticancer therapy remains sparse. The pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cancer-associated fibroblast study provides the strongest resistance-proximal immune-functional evidence, whereas mucinous colorectal extracellular vesicles, ovarian ascites, invasive-front fibroblasts, treatment-remodeled stroma and prognostic signatures require more direct therapy-response validation. Gastric and intestinal epithelial data further caution that PLA2G2A may accompany differentiation, invasion restraint, antimicrobial defense or barrier protection. We therefore argue against treating PLA2G2A as a universal oncogenic target. Instead, it should be advanced as a mechanism-matched biomarker or therapeutic hypothesis only when compartment, biochemical-output, functional and perturbational evidence converge.

items.title: Activated TILs are restricted by iron availability in pancreatic cancer.
Subtype or state? Rethinking the apCAF paradox and fibroblast plasticity in gastrointestinal cancers.
items.abstract: Antigen-presenting cancer-associated fibroblasts (apCAFs), commonly defined by MHC class II molecules, CD74, and related transcriptional programs, exhibit divergent functions across gastrointestinal tumors. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, mesothelium-derived apCAFs promote regulatory T-cell differentiation and suppress effector responses, whereas their abundance in gastric cancer is associated with earlier-stage disease, longer survival, and improved immunotherapy responses. This paradox may reflect microenvironmental context and classifications that conflate transcriptional state, cellular origin, and immune function. apCAFs may therefore represent reversible, context-dependent states defined by origin, MHC class II-restricted antigen presentation, and co-stimulatory capacity. We propose a two-layer model that has not been validated in apCAFs. In this model, the chromatin accessibility of CIITA, CD40, CD80, and CD86 constructs a functional licensing range, while interferon - γ (IFN - γ), interleukin-1 (IL-1), and transforming growth factor - β (TGF - β) guide the formation of specific phenotypes within this range. Insufficient co-stimulation may favor immune tolerance; activation of co-stimulatory programs may support CD4+ T-cell help and CD8+ T-cell infiltration. Treatment-induced changes in CAF composition may reflect selective survival or genuine state transitions. Distinguishing these mechanisms requires lineage tracing, longitudinal single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin profiling, and patient-derived organoid-fibroblast co-cultures. Neoadjuvant therapy and serial endoscopic sampling provide feasible settings for capturing transient states. This framework supports replacing broad CAF depletion with temporally and state-informed functional reprogramming.

items.title: Mechanosensitive YAP-RUNX1 signaling drives TH1 cell dysfunction and tumor immunosuppression.
items.abstract: Tissue stiffening is a predominant malignant physical alteration in cancer progression, yet its effect on specific immune subsets within the tumor microenvironment is not well defined. Here we show that elevated tissue stiffness subverts tumor-infiltrating type 1 helper T (TH1) cells to drive immunosuppression in pancreatic cancer. Mechanistically, stiffness triggers integrin-mediated mechanotransduction to activate YAP, which translocates to the nucleus and cooperates with RUNX1 to transcriptionally upregulate a set of dysfunction-associated genes. These reprogrammed TH1 cells acquire a distinct dysfunction-associated secretory phenotype, which in turn drives M2-like polarization of macrophages and amplifies local immunosuppression. Notably, inhibiting YAP expression or disrupting YAP-RUNX1 interaction reverses the dysfunctional state of TH1 cells and restores antitumor immunity. These findings delineate a mechano-immunological mechanism by which tumor stiffness subverts TH1 cell functions, indicating a possible therapeutic avenue to alleviate immunosuppression and potentiate immunotherapy efficacy in stiff tumors.

items.title: Reply to the Letter to the Editor: Evaluation of P-POSSUM Risk Scoring System in Prediction of Morbidity and Mortality after Pancreaticoduodenectomy.
items.abstract: Dear Editor, As a reply to the Letter to the Editor written by Yasin Alper Yildiz (1), first we are thankful for the interest in our study. We thank the authors for their careful reading of our manuscript and for raising this important methodological issue. We agree that the equations used for the calculation of predicted morbidity and mortality should have been stated more explicitly in the Methods section. For clarification, the physiological score (PS) and operative severity score (OS) were calculated according to the original POSSUM scoring system. items.title: Letter to the Editor: Evaluation of P-POSSUM Risk Scoring System in Prediction of Morbidity and Mortality after Pancreaticoduodenectomy.
items.abstract: Dear Editor, We read with great interest the article by Bodea et al., entitled "Evaluation of P-POSSUM Risk Scoring System in Prediction of Morbidity and Mortality after Pancreaticoduodenectomy" (1). The authors should be congratulated for evaluating perioperative risk prediction in pancreaticoduodenectomy, where accurate estimation of postoperative outcomes remains of considerable clinical importance. i Hwever, we would like to seek clarification regarding the methodology used to estimate postoperative morbidity. /i The authors state that physiological scores, operative severity scores, and the predicted risks of complications and death were calculated using the online calculator available at i http://www.riskprediction.org.uk/index-pp.php /i . Subsequently, the manuscript reports predicted morbidity, observed-to-estimated morbidity ratios (O Morb/E Morb), receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses for morbidity, and discusses the predictive performance of P-POSSUM for postoperative morbidity throughout the Results and Discussion sections.[ a href="https://revistachirurgia.ro/pdfs/2026-5-593.pdf" read more /a ].

items.title: Endoscopic Rendezvous Technique as a Salvage Strategy for Incomplete Pancreas Divisum.
items.abstract: Pancreas divisum (PD) is the most common congenital anomaly of the pancreatic ductal system, resulting from incomplete fusion of the dorsal and ventral pancreatic ducts during embryogenesis and occurring in approximately 5%-10% of the general population. Although most individuals remain asymptomatic, a subset may develop recurrent acute pancreatitis, potentially related to impaired pancreatic drainage through the minor papilla. We report the case of a 55-year-old woman with a 12-year history of recurrent pancreatitis and persistent epigastric pain, in whom an incomplete PD with an impacted pancreatic duct stone was ultimately identified. Initial cross-sectional imaging failed to demonstrate the underlying ductal anomaly. Conventional minor papilla cannulation during endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography was unsuccessful because of the small and edematous papillary orifice. A transpapillary rendezvous technique was subsequently employed to facilitate access to the dorsal pancreatic duct, allowing minor papilla sphincterotomy, stone extraction, and pancreatic duct stent placement. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of incomplete PD and demonstrates a technically demanding endoscopic rescue strategy when conventional minor papilla cannulation fails.

items.title: Recurrent Multi-territory Thromboembolism As the Initial Presentation of Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma and Suspected Nonbacterial Thrombotic Endocarditis.
items.abstract: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE), also known as Marantic endocarditis, is an uncommon complication of malignancy that may cause systemic embolization. We report a 74-year-old woman who developed a right gastrocnemius deep vein thrombosis followed by recurrent right middle cerebral artery occlusions requiring two mechanical thrombectomies. Her subsequent course was complicated by further deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and acute limb ischemia. Repeat echocardiography demonstrated mitral valve vegetations, initially raising concern for infective endocarditis. However, repeated blood cultures and cultures of retrieved thrombotic material were negative. Imaging revealed widespread metastatic disease, and biopsy of a left supraclavicular lymph node confirmed metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The combination of recurrent arterial and venous thrombosis, advanced malignancy, and negative microbiological investigations favored a clinical diagnosis of NBTE. This case illustrates how extensive thromboembolic disease may precede the diagnosis of pancreatic cancer and highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by valvular vegetations in this setting.

items.title: Contact-phagy remodels ER-mitochondria contact sites
items.abstract: Membrane contact sites between the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and other organelles coordinate cellular organization, metabolism and stress responses, yet how these interfaces are selectively remodeled and removed remains poorly understood. Here we identify a selective autophagy pathway that targets defined ER-mitochondria contact-site (ERMCS) subdomains for turnover, a process we term Contact-phagy. The ER-resident chaperone SIGMAR1 forms a functional complex with the ER-phagy receptor CCPG1, and SIGMAR1-CCPG1 nanoclusters define ERMCS-associated sites of autophagy initiation. Contact-phagy is selectively engaged by metabolic and mitochondrial stress and promotes turnover of defined contact-site components without broadly affecting general ER-phagy, mitophagy or bulk autophagy. At these sites, SIGMAR1-CCPG1 function is coupled to mitochondrial fission: MFF promotes DRP1 recruitment to ERMCS, whereas loss of CCPG1 or SIGMAR1 causes abnormal persistence and clustering of DRP1 and MFF, accompanied by altered mitochondrial remodeling. Loss of CCPG1 further disrupts ER-mitochondria organization and mitochondrial function in pancreatic tissue, while pancreatic cancer cells depend on CCPG1 and SIGMAR1 for organelle integrity and bioenergetic capacity. Together, our findings establish Contact-phagy as a selective pathway for the turnover of defined organelle contact site subdomains and suggest a broader principle by which interorganelle interfaces are maintained.

items.title: Management of an incidentally discovered pancreatic neoplasm mimicking an ovarian neoplasm during pregnancy: A case report.
items.abstract:
RATIONALE: Mucinous cystic neoplasms (MCNs) of the pancreas are uncommon tumors that occur during pregnancy, but because MCNs of the pancreas are sex hormone responsive, these tumors can grow rapidly. We report a case of MCN of the pancreas that was diagnosed during pregnancy.
PATIENT CONCERNS: A 19.4 × 14.5 cm lesion was detected in the left upper abdomen in a 36-year-old asymptomatic woman with chronic hypertension and diet-controlled gestational diabetes at a gestational age (GA) of 36 weeks.
DIAGNOSES: Magnetic resonance imaging showed a multiseptated cystic mass with a regular thin wall arising from the pancreatic tail, and final pathological findings identified a pancreatic MCN with high-grade neoplasia and no metastasis.
INTERVENTIONS: At a GA of 37+2 weeks, acute severe hypertension raised suspicion for superimposed preeclampsia, and cesarean delivery was performed. Laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy was performed 11 weeks postpartum.
OUTCOMES: The postoperative course was uncomplicated, and a 6-month follow-up was planned without further treatment.
LESSONS: The optimal timing of surgical resection for MCNs of the pancreas in pregnancy should be determined by the GA and the potential for malignancy. If malignancy is not suspected, planned postpartum resection is a safe approach.

items.title: Perihilar Co-Ablation for Pancreatic Cancer Liver Metastasis Adjacent to the Hepatic Pedicle: A Case Report and Literature Review.
items.abstract: Percutaneous ultrasound-guided thermal ablation has become an established treatment modality for liver tumors, providing advantages such as minimal invasiveness, reliable local tumor control, and rapid recovery. However, tumors located near the hepatic pedicle pose a major technical challenge. The hepatic pedicle, comprising the hepatic artery, portal vein, and bile duct, is highly vulnerable to thermal injury. Conventional ablation in this region carries significant risks of iatrogenic biliary stenosis, vascular injury, segmental hepatic ischemia, and liver insufficiency.We report the case of a 55-year-old man who underwent distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy for moderately differentiated pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (maximum diameter, 3.8 cm). Postoperative pathological examination revealed perineural invasion and intravascular tumor thrombus. Follow-up imaging showed a metastatic lesion in the right hepatic lobe immediately adjacent to the right hepatic pedicle. Given the challenging tumor location and the patient's prior surgical history, percutaneous ablation was considered a favorable treatment option. However, the risk of thermal injury to the hepatic pedicle using a conventional ablation trajectory was unacceptably high. Therefore, we developed a novel technique, termed "perihilar co-ablation", using the Co-ablation System. Under ultrasound guidance, the ablation probe was advanced along a safe perihilar trajectory, taking advantage of real-time ice-ball visualization to achieve complete tumor ablation while the adjacent hepatic pedicle structures were not damaged. Post-ablation imaging demonstrated complete coverage of the tumor by the ablation zone, with no residual tumor present, and the hepatic pedicle structure was also preserved.The patient recovered uneventfully and was discharged on postoperative day 2. At the 6-month follow-up, no tumor recurrence or procedure-related complications were observed. This perihilar co-ablation technique may be applicable to patients who were originally deemed unsuitable for or at high risk for traditional ablation treatments. Larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are required to evaluate its safety and efficacy.
